existing_roles.title: Plant Manager
existing_roles.description:
Description:

The Plant Manager is responsible for all Operations employees within the facility. The Plant Manager is also responsible for managing all tasks related to the maintenance of the building. The Plant Manager distributes and monitors the workload within the Operations areas, while maintaining the highest level of quality and productivity possible. The Plant Manager will make sure that all instructions are thoroughly followed, and that accurate documentation is recorded correctly for all work produced. This role will demonstrate highly effective and advanced time management, organizational and planning capabilities, strong attention to efficiency and provide exceptional internal and external customer satisfaction.

Requirements:

Other duties may be assigned as needed.

* Read, interpret, and understand the work order completely and plan work to ensure meeting of customer specifications, including reviewing materials that operators are going to use for as specified on the work order.
* Distribute work to each machine with a focus on how long it should take the operator to complete the assigned work and with a focus on what work is a priority.
* Ensure completion of jobs in a timely manner, meeting quantity requirements and maintaining a high degree of quality in all work performed.
* Effectively communicate status of equipment and work in process to VP-Operations.
* Check daily reports to ensure that reprints are being completed in a timely manner and that work orders are being closed in a timely manner.
* Check daily reports to ensure that all postage receipts are done completely and in a timely manner.
* Run end of shift reports with the use of Clarity and OPALS.
* Work with vendors to maintain equipment regarding preventive maintenance and down machines.
* Make recommendations to improve workflow, quality, efficiency, and safety: in turn reducing operating problems and improving product quality within the manufacturing area.
* Enforce all safety rules are being followed during the operation, maintenance, set-up, changing parts, or any other activity taking place.
* Enforce that no employee ever removes, disables, or otherwise tampers with the function of any safety devices installed on company property or equipment. Notify management immediately if you suspect any safety device to be malfunctioning, broken, or missing.
* Keep accurate records of work performed and materials used in accordance with Content Critical Solutions procedures.
* Enforce the return of all tools and accessories used to their proper location clean and in good condition.
* Enforce that all employees maintain a neat and orderly area. Assist in general housekeeping in common areas.
* Treat coworkers with respect and courtesy.
* Perform all reasonable requests from upper management.
* Read, understand, and comply with all written work instructions.
* Work as a team and participate in Content Critical Solutions efforts to ensure continuous improvement of processes, methodologies, productivity, and quality while reducing costs.
* Manage all tasks related to the maintenance of the building.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* This job has management responsibilities over all Operations employees in the facility.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* Able to understand written and verbal instructions in English.
* Able to handle a rapidly paced work environment.

**EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE**

* High School diploma or GED.
* Prior experience working in direct mail manufacturing preferred but not required.
* Prior experience managing a facility preferred but not required.
* Knowledgeable in Microsoft Office Suite.

**LANGUAGE SKILLS**

* Ability to read and comprehend instructions, correspondences, and memos.
* Ability to verbally communicate effectively with coworkers and upper management.

**MATHEMATICAL SKILLS**

* Ability to perform simple addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.

existing_roles.title: VP Quality Assurance and Safety
existing_roles.description:
**Compensation Range**

$240,000 - $280,000 / Year

**Overview**

**At The Cheesecake Factory Bakery, We Don't Do Ordinary!** Nothing is scaled down. Not the pride, not the fun, and definitely not the teamwork. Here, you’ll have the opportunity to shape the future of our Bakery business, lead great people, and strengthen the systems behind the iconic cheesecakes our guests have loved for decades.

**As the VP, Quality Assurance & Food Safety**, you’ll report to the Bakery President and lead food safety, quality assurance, sanitation, and technical services across two bakery plants totaling more than 160,000 square feet and supporting more than 600 staff members. This is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact: setting the strategy, rebuilding organizational trust, strengthening audit readiness, and elevating Good Manufacturing Practices through disciplined root cause analysis and corrective action. You’ll operate at both the executive and plant levels, bringing the leadership, technical expertise, and influence needed to create lasting change.

**You’ll thrive in this position if you are:**

* **A Trusted Executive Leader:** You build credibility through transparency, sound judgment, and consistent follow-through, earning the confidence to influence decisions at every level.
* **A Strategic, Hands-On Quality Leader:** You set the vision while staying connected to operations, understanding risk, removing barriers, and translating strategy into consistent execution.
* **An Audit and Compliance Expert:** You build a culture of year-round readiness where issues are identified early, corrective actions are effective, and findings are sustainably closed.
* **A Disciplined Problem Solver:** You look beyond the immediate issue, using data, risk assessment, and root cause analysis to solve systemic problems and prevent recurrence.

**Responsibilities**

* Set and lead the Bakery division’s Quality Assurance and Food Safety strategy across both facilities, establishing clear expectations for risk management, performance, and accountability.
* Serve as a trusted advisor to the Bakery President and executive leadership, providing clear perspective on food safety and quality risks, audit readiness, significant incidents, and corrective actions.
* Ensure trust and confidence in the function through technical credibility, transparency, strong partnerships, and consistent execution.
* Strengthen compliance and operational discipline across GMPs, HACCP, SQF, AIB, sanitation, allergen controls, environmental monitoring, traceability, supplier quality, microbiological testing, and recall readiness.
* Establish sustained audit readiness and ensure findings have clear ownership, effective corrective actions, and lasting resolution.
* Ensure highly systematic and disciplined adherence to product and process standards on a real-time basis to guarantee our cakes are beautiful and delicious.
* Build greater rigor around root cause analysis and corrective and preventive actions, addressing systemic issues rather than symptoms.
* Provide leadership across product and process quality, customer complaints, foreign-material controls, product holds, specifications, labeling, formulas, recipes, and Technical Services.
* Establish meaningful metrics and use data to identify trends, prioritize risk, and hold the organization accountable for results.
* Lead significant food safety, quality, sanitation, and regulatory matters with urgency, sound judgment, and appropriate escalation.
* Build and develop a high-performing Quality Assurance, Food Safety, Sanitation, and Technical Services organization with the talent and capabilities needed for long-term success.
* Partner with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Research and Development, and Human Resources to strengthen ownership and accountability for food safety and quality across the business.
* Prioritize resources and investments against the greatest risks and opportunities while effectively managing the function’s budget.

**Qualifications**

* 15+ years of progressive leadership experience in Quality Assurance, Food Safety, Sanitation, or Technical Services within food manufacturing, including senior-level, multi-site responsibility.
* Demonstrated success leading food safety and quality strategy, organizational transformation, culture improvement, and high-performing technical teams.
* Deep expertise in GMPs, HACCP, preventive controls, sanitation, microbiological risk, allergen management, environmental monitoring, traceability, recalls, supplier quality, AIB, SQF, and food safety management systems.
* Extensive experience leading regulatory, certification, customer, and internal audits from preparation through corrective action and sustainable closure.
* Expertise in root cause analysis, corrective and preventive action, risk assessment, and incident investigation.
* Proven ability to build organizational trust, strengthen accountability, influence senior leaders, and lead through significant change.

* Must be able to prioritize and manage resources to achieve projects results even when time and/or resources are constrained.

To perform the job successfully, an individual should demonstrate the following competencies:

Demonstrates group presentation skills working in a global environment; actively participates in meetings providing clear information.

**Who we are and what we value:**

Feed Energy works at the intersection of feed, fuel, and agriculture, building a nearly four-decade legacy of stewardship across the industries we serve. We support how America nourishes its people and powers its economy. Our team is made up of growth-minded individuals dedicated to transforming global practices in feeding and fueling. We create circular economies through sustainable, low-carbon products and processes. Join us if you are looking for a dynamic environment where you can help shape a more sustainable future.

**We help feed the world by providing safe, energy-based nutrition solutions.**

Creativity • Stewardship • Impact • Integrity • Healthy Relationships

**What we are looking for:**The Head of Plant Operations is a highly visible, hands-on leader responsible for operational performance across all Feed Energy manufacturing facilities. This role leads Plant Managers and the Senior Operations Support Manager, establishes consistent operating standards, and ensures the plants function as one integrated operating system.The Head of Plant Operations owns the execution of safety, quality, production, cost, reliability, and continuous improvement priorities across all locations. A key focus of the position is developing plant leadership capability, reinforcing accountability, and building the operating discipline required to deliver consistent results. This position reports to the Chief Operations Officer and requires up to 60% travel.

**What you will do:**

* Lead day-to-day operational execution across Feed Energy’s four manufacturing locations.
* Own plant performance targets, including throughput, yield, uptime, labor efficiency, cost per unit, and total operating cost.
* Establish consistent daily, weekly, and monthly operating routines, KPI reporting, and escalation processes.
* Maintain a visible presence on plant floors by observing work, coaching leaders, supporting problem-solving, and building relationships with frontline employees.
* Manage Plant Managers and the Senior Operations Support Manager, setting clear expectations and reinforcing accountability for results.
* Develop Plant Managers, supervisors, and frontline leaders through coaching, feedback, and hands-on leadership support.
* Manage plant operating expenses, including labor, maintenance, utilities, consumables, and outside services, within the approved operational budget.
* Partner with Finance on expense forecasting, variance management, and operating cost inputs for capital planning.
* Lead the daily execution of safety and environmental programs in partnership with the Environmental Health and Safety team.
* Uphold product quality standards and partner with Quality to reduce defects, product holds, and customer quality concerns.
* Build and enforce consistent operating standards and standard operating procedures across all locations.
* Eliminate unnecessary differences in processes, practices, and performance between plants.
* Apply Lean, Six Sigma, root cause analysis, and structured problem-solving as part of daily operations.
* Coordinate operational priorities across Engineering, Maintenance, Quality, Supply Chain, Logistics, Finance, and Culture and Talent.
* Model servant leadership and build a culture of safety, ownership, accountability, development, and continuous improvement.
* Demonstrate Feed Energy company values in all everyday work interactions.
* Perform other duties as assigned.

Requirements:

**What you will need:**

* At least 10 years of progressive leadership experience in manufacturing operations.
* Proven experience directly leading multi-site operations, including three or more facilities.
* Demonstrated success building and implementing operating systems across multiple locations.
* Experience managing operating expenses and delivering cost performance within budget.
* Strong experience coaching and developing Plant Managers, operations leaders, supervisors, and frontline teams.

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations Management, or a related field.

* Experience in feed, food, chemical, lipid, or other process-manufacturing environments.

* Experience scaling operations during organizational growth or technology transitions.

**WHO WE ARE**  
At Ghirardelli, we honor tradition and drive innovation, aiming to be the top choice for premium chocolate. We support personal and professional growth, recognizing that each employee’s contribution directly impacts Ghirardelli’s growth and success. Join our dynamic team and help shape Ghirardelli's future.

**Job Summary**

The Head of Production is accountable for safe, compliant, reliable, and cost-effective production across all three shifts of the factory. This role leads the production organization, establishes consistent operating standards and management routines across shifts, and ensures delivery of safety, food safety, quality, service, cost, productivity, waste, and people objectives.

The Head of Production translates factory strategy into clear production priorities, develops leadership capability throughout the production organization, creates the accountability required for sustained execution and deliver on key organizational metrics. The role partners and collaborates cross-functionally to resolve systemic losses, strengthen operating discipline, improve asset and labor performance, and embed TPM and continuous improvement practices into daily operations.

  
  

* Establish and sustain a culture of Safety and Food Safety, shifting the mindset to one of immediate intervention, learning, correction, and prevention of unsafe behaviors or conditions.
* Ensure production leaders visibly demonstrate safety and food-safety leadership on every shift
* Ensure timely containment, investigation, corrective action, and verification following significant incidents or deviations
* Partner with Safety and Quality to ensure standards are understood, implemented, audited, and sustained
* Ensure production readiness for internal, customer, and regulatory audits
* Lead, coach, and develop the production team to ensure clear expectations, accountability, and effective succession plans
* Establish consistent leadership expectations and operating discipline across all three shifts
* Ensure recognition, coaching, corrective action, and performance management are applied consistently across shifts
* Create an environment where standards are understood, leaders address deviations promptly, and follow-through is visible
* Identify systemic losses and ensure effective corrective and preventive actions are implemented
* Sponsor cross-functional improvement teams addressing systemic production losses
* Lead the AM pillar implementation into the culture and mindset of the factory
* Verify that corrective actions address root causes and prevent recurrence across applicable shifts and production areas
* Drive recovery plans when production performance deviates from plan
* Manage production spending, labor, overtime, material variances, and productivity commitments
* Ensure production capacity, labor capability, and operating constraints are represented in annual and long-term planning
* Partner with Maintenance and Reliability to align production plans, preventive maintenance, equipment access, shutdown execution, and chronic-loss elimination
* Partner with Planning and Warehouse to align production schedules, material availability, inventory requirements, and service priorities
* Partner with Quality to manage holds, deviations, and release priorities
* Partner with Engineering on design reviews, commissioning, qualifications, start-up, stabilization, and operational handoff of capital projects
* Partner with Training on workforce planning, leadership capability, and capability development plans
* Partner with HR and factory leadership on labor relations, grievance resolution, contract administration, negotiations, mediation, and arbitration, as required.
* Hire, develop and manage performance of team. Create an inclusive environment that embraces our values and purpose.
* Ensure reconciliation of production workorders and partner with finance function to reconcile and resolve any losses
* Partner with IP team for execution of projects to systematically reduce waste across processing and packaging streams
* Enable a proactive, positive, collaborative and engaged culture across all levels of the production organization
* Complete special projects and other duties as assigned or as necessary.
  

  

Minimum Education and Experience

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, operations management, food science, supply chain, business, or a related field
* 10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience in a complex, multi-shift operation
* Experience leading managers and an organization with multiple levels of leadership
* Demonstrated accountability for safety, quality, service, cost, productivity and people results
* Experience in food, beverage, consumer packaged goods, or another regulated manufacturing environment
* Working knowledge of food-safety systems, manufacturing quality systems, and applicable regulatory requirements
* Experience applying Lean, TPM, or another structured continuous-improvement system
* Experience with labor planning, operating budgets, and performance management
* Ability to lead effectively in a union-represented environment
  

  

Other Job Requirements

* Regular presence in manufacturing and production areas is required
* Flexibility to work across all three shifts to provide leadership visibility, conduct reviews, coach leaders, and respond to operational needs.
* Availability outside of normal business hours for significant safety, food safety, quality, people, equipment, or service events
* Ability to operate in manufacturing environments involving noise, heat, cold, moving equipment, stairs, elevated areas, and required PPE
* Limited travel may be required for business meetings, training, supplier visits, benchmarking, or project support

Ghirardelli's salary range reflects market rates based on our size, revenue, and location. Starting pay is determined using a wide range of factors including, but not limited to, job-related skills, knowledge, and experience as well as market conditions. existing_roles.description:
**About Monster Energy:**
-------------------------

Forget about blending in. That's not our style. We're the risk-takers, the trailblazers, the game-changers. We're not perfect, and we don't pretend to be. We're raw, unfiltered, and a bit unconventional. But our drive is unrivaled, just like our athletes. The power is in your hands to define what success looks like and where you want to take your career. It's not just about what we do, but about who we become along the way. We are much more than a brand here. We are a way of life, a mindset. Join us.

**A day in the life:**
----------------------

As the Director, SAP Supply Chain Planning & Manufacturing Systems, you will own the design, implementation, and optimization of Monster's end-to-end supply chain planning landscape within the SAP ecosystem. Your primary focus is SAP Integrated Business Planning (IBP) covering demand planning, supply planning, S&OP, inventory optimization, order based planning and the roadmap of S/4HANA.

You will also guide the connected Manufacturing and Quality solutions, including SAP PP, PP/DS, production execution, and SAP QM, so that planning decisions flow cleanly into the plant floor and quality processes. You will set global processes, solution architecture, and governance; lead a team of SAP IT professionals; and partner with Supply Chain, Operations, and Quality leaders to drive continuous improvement and innovation.

**The impact you'll make:**
---------------------------

***Supply Chain Planning (primary focus)***

* Own the global SAP planning solution, with SAP IBP and SAP APO (DP, SNP, PP/DS) as the core platforms, and define the target architecture and roadmap, including to S/4HANA.
* Lead solution design and configuration decisions across demand planning, supply planning, S&OP, inventory optimization, and response/deployment planning.
* Lead planning projects from inception to completion, including implementations, upgrades, enhancements, and migrations, delivered on time, in scope, and on budget.
* Establish planning master data standards, parameter governance, and integration between IBP/APO, S/4HANA, and connected systems (e.g., RTI, CPI).
* Serve as the point of contact on emerging trends in supply chain planning and evaluate solutions that improve forecast accuracy, service levels, and inventory performance.

***Manufacturing & Quality (supporting scope)***

* Oversee SAP production execution solutions so that plans translate into executable production schedules across plants and co-manufacturers.
* Guide SAP QM processes, including inspection planning, batch management, quality notifications, and release, in partnership with Quality and Regulatory teams.
* Ensure end-to-end integration across Planning, Manufacturing, and Quality so the business runs on one consistent process.

***Leadership & strategy***

* Analyze business requirements, prioritize based on cost/benefit, and present a clear implementation roadmap to IT and business leadership.
* Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing global team of SAP specialists and manage system integrator and partner relationships.
* Partner closely with end-to-end solution verticals to understand requirements, manage business risk, and deliver quality outcomes on budget and timeline.
* Engage operations leaders to identify problems suited to AI, automation, and advanced analytics, in line with the Digital Transformation (DT) roadmap and vision.

**Who you are:**
----------------

* Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Information Technology, Business Administration, or a related field preferred.
* 10+ years of SAP supply chain experience working on the IT side, including hands-on process mapping, solution design, configuration, and customization.
* **7+ years of hands-on SAP IBP and/or SAP APO experience**, including at least one full-lifecycle implementation you led or owned. APO-to-IBP migration experience strongly preferred.
* Working experience with SAP PP, and production execution, and exposure to SAP QM. Depth here is valued but secondary to Planning.
* Experience with SAP S/4HANA and SAP SCM implementations as part of an IT team.
* Proven track record making solution design and roadmap decisions and leading SAP teams and system integrators.
* Experience aligning teams to a common business process and driving application adoption.

***Preferred***

* Certifications: SAP IBP, APICS (CPIM/CSCP), SAP Manufacturing, or SAP Quality.
* Experience in consumer packaged goods, beverage, or other high-volume manufacturing environments.
* Background with automation and analytics tools and platforms (e.g., RPA, workflow automation, process mining, AI/ML forecasting).
* Technical skills: SAP IBP, SAP APO (DP, SNP, PP/DS), S/4HANA, SAP PP, SAP QM, SAP Analytics Cloud, and Microsoft tools.

existing_roles.description:
**At Carbon, our mission goes beyond 3D printing. We are enabling creators everywhere to make what the world needs, right now. Our company is built on the idea that diverse fields of study must come together to solve intractable problems. We have grand ambitions to create technology that will influence industry around the world. You will be joining a diverse team with a vibrant culture, where team success is as important as celebrating individual contributions.**

  

**Help us change the world and we will help you change yours.**

  

**Job Description:**

  

We are seeking a Head of Production & Supply Chain Operations to lead our Hardware Production Team and the end-to-end logistics and inventory function that keeps Carbon’s global supply chain running. This role is critical to scaling our production operations while maintaining our commitment to safety, quality, and cost efficiency, while ensuring the accuracy, compliance, and reliable flow of Carbon’s inventory and freight worldwide. The ideal candidate is a disciplined, detail-oriented leader who thrives in a hands-on manufacturing environment, knows how to build, inspire, and motivate high-performing teams, and can operate effectively across both production and supply chain disciplines. Reporting to the Director of Supply Chain, this individual will own the end-to-end production process and the logistics and inventory organization, driving continuous improvement and ensuring our products and materials meet the highest standards from supplier to customer.

  

***This role will be spending time at both our Thomas Rd, Santa Clara and Borregas Ave, Sunnyvale locations and you will be expected to be in-office 5 days per week.***

  

**What You Will Do**

  

**Team Leadership & Development**

* Recruit, hire, onboard, and develop a team of manufacturing technicians and logistics and inventory staff, building a culture rooted in accountability, pride in craftsmanship, and continuous learning.
* Set clear performance expectations and conduct regular coaching sessions, performance reviews, and skills assessments to elevate individual and team capabilities across production and logistics/inventory functions.
* Foster a positive, motivated work environment where team members feel valued and engaged, resulting in strong retention and morale.
Create training programs and cross-training plans to ensure workforce flexibility and depth across all production stations and logistics/inventory operations.  

  

**Safety**

* Champion a safety-first culture across the production floor and logistics and warehouse operations, ensuring compliance with all OSHA regulations and company safety policies.
* Conduct regular safety audits, risk assessments, and incident investigations; implement corrective and preventive actions promptly.
* Develop, maintain, and enforce standard operating procedures (SOPs) that prioritize operator and warehouse safety in every task.
Track and report safety metrics, driving toward zero-incident goals through proactive hazard identification and mitigation.  

  

**Quality**

* Own product quality throughout the manufacturing and assembly process, ensuring every product meets rigorous quality standards before shipment.
* Implement and manage quality control checkpoints, inspection protocols, and testing procedures at critical stages of production.
* Collaborate with Ops Engineering and Quality teams to resolve defects, perform root cause analysis, and drive corrective actions.
Monitor yield rates and first-pass quality metrics, using data to drive continuous improvement initiatives.  

  

**Cost & Operational Efficiency**

* Manage production budgets, labor costs, and material utilization to meet or exceed cost targets without compromising safety or quality.
* Own budget and cost outcomes for Carbon’s freight, logistics, and inventory programs.
* Identify and implement process improvements using Lean manufacturing principles to reduce waste, improve throughput, and increase efficiency.
* Plan and manage production schedules, capacity, and resource allocation to meet delivery commitments and customer demand.
Partner with Strategic Sourcing and Planning to optimize inventory levels and ensure timely availability of components and materials.  

  

**Logistics & Inventory Leadership**

* Own management accountability for the cost, service levels, and integrity of Carbon’s global goods flow, including all inbound and outbound freight and global inventory accuracy and compliance.
* Lead, mentor, and directly manage the team of inventory and logistics staff, setting priorities and building scalable processes as Carbon grows.
* Ensure full compliance with international trade regulations and dangerous goods/hazardous materials requirements.
Establish and track logistics and inventory KPIs (cost per shipment, on-time delivery, inventory accuracy, freight as a percentage of revenue) and drive continuous improvement against them.  

  

**Cross-Functional Collaboration & Reporting**

* Serve as the primary liaison between the production floor and the Engineering, Supply Chain, and Quality teams to ensure seamless product launches and design-for-manufacturability feedback.
* Serve as the primary management point of contact for Finance, Legal, EH&S, Sales, contract manufacturing partners, and 3PLs on logistics, inventory, and trade compliance matters.
* Participate in new product introduction processes, contributing manufacturing insights during design reviews and pilot builds.
Provide regular production, logistics, and inventory status reports, KPIs, and escalation updates to senior leadership.  

  

**Qualifications**

  

**Required:**

* 8+ years of experience in a manufacturing or production management role, with demonstrated success leading teams of technicians or production operators.
* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related field.
* Experience managing, overseeing, or working closely with logistics, freight, and inventory functions, including leading teams responsible for freight and inventory control.
* Proven ability to build, develop, and motivate high-performing teams in a hands-on manufacturing environment, with a track record of maintaining safe production environments.
* Strong technical aptitude with the ability to understand complex electromechanical assemblies and manufacturing processes.
* Demonstrated discipline and meticulous attention to detail in managing production operations, documentation, and quality systems.
* Experience managing budgets, schedules, and resource planning.
Excellent communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills, including the ability to partner effectively with a senior individual-contributor expert to translate strategy into team execution.  

  

**Nice to Have:**

* Understanding of workplace safety regulations (OSHA).
* Lean manufacturing certification (e.g., Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt).
* Experience with ISO 9001 or similar quality management systems.
* Background in 3D printing, additive manufacturing, or precision hardware production.
* Experience with ERP/MRP systems and production tracking tools.
* Familiarity with Design for Manufacturing (DFM) and Design for Assembly (DFA) principles.
Familiarity with international trade compliance and dangerous goods/hazardous materials regulations.  

  

*You do not need to match every listed expectation to apply for this position. Here at Carbon, we know that diverse perspectives foster the innovation we need to be successful, and we are committed to building a team that encompasses a variety of backgrounds, experiences, and skills.*

**Department Information**
--------------------------

The mission of the Colorado Energy Office (CEO) is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and consumer energy costs by advancing clean energy, energy efficiency, and zero emission vehicles to benefit all Coloradans. We do this by developing and implementing highly impactful policies and programs, establishing Colorado as a leading state for climate action. The Colorado Energy Office is a great place to work, with collaborative and talented employees who are passionate about our mission and a hybrid atmosphere. Employees report high satisfaction with their work, their colleagues and manager, and CEO leadership. Join us!

  
  

Reducing greenhouse gas pollution and advancing zero emission vehicles, energy efficiency and clean energy are essential to preserving and protecting Colorado’s way of life. These actions defend the health of our communities and natural environment, provide access to lower cost clean energy resources for rural and urban areas, increase investment and economic growth opportunities, and expand clean energy jobs. As part of our mission we serve the people of Colorado with programs focusing on weatherization, energy efficiency, and electric vehicles and a regulatory and legislative agenda to promote the interests of all Coloradans.

  
  

***We are committed to increasing the diversity of our staff and providing culturally responsive programs and services. Therefore, we encourage responses from people of all backgrounds and abilities.***

**Description of Job**
----------------------

* **This is a hybrid position. Hybrid positions are required to be present at the office location for a minimum of two days per work week during the first 90 days, and minimum one to two days a week after that, or as directed by office leadership.**

CEO’s Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP), helps qualified Coloradans save money, increase comfort, and better their homes and environment through proven energy conservation solutions.These solutions include LED light bulbs, high efficiency furnaces and refrigerators, building shell insulation, and rooftop solar arrays, among others.

  
  

CEO is hiring for a visionary Senior Manager, Weatherization Quality & Technical Services to join the WAP team. You will serve as a strategic leader, bridging advanced building science with organizational excellence. This role is pivotal in shaping how we deliver sustainable energy solutions to diverse communities across Colorado, turning technical compliance into a platform for continuous improvement and innovation.

The WAP network spans all 64 Colorado counties, delivering critical energy efficiency and clean energy solutions to diverse populations through a network of six subgrantee agencies. As the Senior Manager, you will step into a high-impact, supervisory role overseeing a team of technical experts located around the state who serve as the definitive authority on residential building science, ensuring weatherization work meets performance standards through on-site inspections, detailed reporting, and training, while also acting as an internal and network consultant to streamline operations, drive process improvement, and ensure program delivery is transparent and visible.

  
  

In this senior-level manager capacity, you will blend advanced building science knowledge with administrative leadership and process optimization.

WAP Specific Duties and Responsibilities

* Lead the Quality Management team, which includes Technical & QCI Quality Management staff in completing all necessary BPI certified Quality Assurance Inspections (typically 50-75/yr) and Quality Control visits (typically 20-30/yr) across Colorado to meet all federal and state statutory and programmatic requirements
* Balance the team’s core focus (QA, QC, & training) with opportunities for ongoing innovation.
* Drive strategic quality management through Quality Control and Assurance (QC & QA), transforming federal guidelines into accessible, actionable insights that empower our subgrantee network
* Cultivate a high-performing team by providing mentorship and leadership that fosters a collaborative, inclusive environment where technical experts can thrive and innovate
* Partner with other CEO WAP teams to integrate quality management operational outcomes with targeted training to drive continuous, lasting enhancements across the program
* Lead the QM team in partnering with other CEO WAP teams to develop and deliver targeted, hands-on guidance to local subgrantee organizations undergoing leadership shifts or performance remediation, ensuring full alignment with state and federal guidelines, state program implementation strategies, and complementary clean energy initiatives
* Champion Operational Excellence by collaborating cross-functionally with other CEO WAP teams to identify bottlenecks, modernize our workflows, and scale our program’s reach
* Provide immediate support to subgrantees to address critical safety hazards detected during site evaluations or staff reviews, escalating severe concerns to WAP Director when subgrantee remediation or corrective action is warranted
* Work with the rest of the WAP team on QM production metrics from subgrantee agencies, auditing subgrantee performance for integrity and collaborating cross-functionally to report key outcomes to program leadership, federal partners, state administrators, and legislative bodies
* Influence Program Strategy by serving as a key advisor in creating WAP policy, translating real-world QM data into meaningful policy updates that increase program equity and effectiveness
* Modernize Tooling by leading the integration and management of platforms like monday.com to create transparent, streamlined project tracking systems and program delivery improvements.
* Participate in national and regional WAP events hosted by national associations to learn from and elevate the work of Colorado WAP

General Duties and Responsibilities

* Adhere to all technical and health and safety policies and procedures in the planning and execution of activities
* Maintain positive working relationships with a diverse range of stakeholders including WAP subgrantee agency staff, CEO Ops and Finance team, Federal Department of Energy partners, among others
* Abide by office policies and procedures in a manner that ensures fiscal responsibility and promotes efficient, effective, and elegant government.
* Use application software (i.e. word processing, spreadsheet, database, project management software, etc.) to prepare correspondence, plans, reports, schedules, and other documents
* Assist other CEO departments in carrying out unit and office wide priorities.
* Perform other duties as requested and required

**Supplemental Information**
----------------------------

We are looking for an experienced manager who pairs technical building science awareness with sophisticated team leadership expertise and continuous improvement approach.

Minimum Qualifications

* Minimum 2 years of direct supervisory experience OR similar translatable experience (indirect supervision like volunteer management, mentorship, vendor or contractor management)
* Minimum three years of working, inspection, and/or training experience in weatherization, residential energy efficiency services, or closely related field

Skills and Knowledge  
  

* Demonstrated ability to use the virtual collaboration strategies and tools necessary to lead a distributed team
* Demonstrated experience tracking compliance, reviewing staff reporting, and processing/approving invoices
* Dedicated to continuous improvement, desire to learn new skills
* Demonstrated leadership and facilitation capabilities
* Strong organizational skills and attention to detail
* Strong interpersonal skills with a focus on developing strong relationships
* Ability to independently start and finish tasks
* Ability to work independently and as part of a team
* Strong written, oral, and presentation communication skills
* Willingness to adapt to and enhance current team culture
* Proficient in the following:

  + Google Suite (Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive, Gmail, Calendar, etc.) or Microsoft equivalent
  + Video conferencing software (Zoom, Google Meet, MS Teams, etc.)
* Experience and/or a willingness to use AI tools and best practices to inform programs and program management.

Preferred Qualifications

* Direct supervisory experience in the last five years
* Possession of or ability to obtain the Quality Control Inspector (QCI) certification within twelve months of hire date, see this PDF download for more information
* Experience using Salesforce
* Project Management software experience (i.e. Monday.com, Asana, etc.)
* Professional experience in sustainability, climate policy, or clean energy

  
Interested in learning more about:

* Process Improvement Methodologies (i.e Lean/Six Sigma)
* Total Quality Management (TQM)
* Colorado Energy Industry

existing_roles.title: Manufacturing Quality Senior Manager
existing_roles.description:
**Job Description:**

The Senior Manager, Manufacturing Quality builds and leads the quality system supporting Harris' manufacturing network. This role owns quality and certifications across multiple facilities, including the ISO 9001 and ASME (non-nuclear) certification programs, inspection and hold/release, and independent verification of VDC deliverables, so products leave Harris' shops conforming to customer, code, and specification requirements.

  

This role builds and leads the plant-level QA/QC team, who will report directly to it. It holds quality stop-work authority and provides independent verification across facilities. The Senior Manager partners with the Harris corporate QA/QC program, applying and extending it to manufacturing, and works with Manufacturing Operations, Engineering and VDC, Supply Chain, Industrial Engineering, and Safety. The role standardizes quality practices and supports certification of new facilities as the network scales.

  
  

**Core Responsibilities**

  

**Quality Management System & Certifications**

* Own the manufacturing certification programs, including ISO 9001 and ASME, with documentation, internal audits, and management review.
* Lead certification and recertification for new and existing facilities, including customer and third-party audits.
* Align manufacturing procedures with the Harris corporate QMS manual and manage manufacturing-specific procedures and records.
* Drive consistent quality system implementation across the network.
* Represent Harris in professional and industry organizations.
  

**Plant QA/QC Leadership & Inspection**

* Build, staff, and lead the plant-level QA/QC team, including roles, hiring, training, and standards.
* Establish and own inspection, verification, and hold/release processes, from receiving through final inspection.
* Define inspection plans and travelers by product and customer requirement.
* Ensure welding procedures and welder qualifications meet code, and manage calibration of inspection equipment.
* Manage third-party inspection firms and their scope, schedule, and results
  

**VDC Deliverable QA/QC Review**

* Spot-check VDC deliverables, including drawings, models, and BOMs, before they reach the shop, as an independent check on VDC's own QA/QC.
* Audit VDC's QA/QC process and record results, and raise gaps with VDC leadership.
* Track shop-found drawing, model, and BOM issues, and feed trends back to VDC and Engineering.
* Hold deliverables that fail verification until corrected.
  

**Nonconformance, Corrective Action & Quality Performance**

* Own the nonconformance (NCR) process, root cause analysis, and corrective and preventive actions, including supplier issues.
* Track and report quality metrics, including rework, weld repair, NCR trends, and customer complaints.
* Work with Industrial Engineering and plant leadership to turn quality data into improvements.
  

**Quality Stop-Work Authority**

* Exercise stop-work authority when product, process, or documentation does not meet requirements, escalating to the SVP as needed.
* Define clear criteria for stop, hold, and release.
  

**Production Readiness & Supplier Quality**

* Set quality requirements, inspection and test plans, and documentation for new products and projects at the production readiness gate and manage 3rd party inspection companies.
* Partner with Supply Chain on supplier quality, receiving inspection, and material certifications.
* Support customer quality requirements and audits for external customers.
  

**Cross-Functional Collaboration**

This role works closely with:

* Harris corporate QA/QC program leadership
* Manufacturing Operations, Industrial Engineering, Safety
* Engineering, VDC, and Product Engineering
* Supply Chain, Purchasing, and Fulfillment & Logistics
* Manufacturing Business Development and Estimating
* Customers, auditors, and certification bodies
  

The Senior Manager owns the manufacturing quality system and independent verification. Plant leadership owns producing quality product in the shop.

  
  

**Required Qualifications**

* Experience building and leading quality assurance or quality control across multiple manufacturing, fabrication, or prefabrication facilities, including hiring and developing quality staff.
* Experience leading ISO 9001 and ASME or other code-based certification and recertification, including internal audits and corrective action.
* Experience with inspection, nonconformance management, and root cause analysis.
* Ability to read engineering drawings, specifications, and codes.
* Ability to hold plant leaders accountable while keeping production moving.
* Strong communication skills with customers, auditors, and cross-functional teams.
  

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with nuclear quality assurance, ASME boiler and pressure vessel code, or other code-based quality programs.
* Professional Engineer (PE) license.
* Experience with welding, piping, structural, or modular MEP fabrication.
* Certifications such as CWI, ASQ CQE/CQA/CMQ, or Lead Auditor.
* Experience with quality and production tracking systems such as STRATUS.
  

  

**What This Role Is (and Is Not)**

**This role is:**

* The enterprise owner of the manufacturing quality system and certifications.
* The builder and leader of plant-level QA/QC across facilities.
* The authority for inspection, hold/release, and quality stop-work.
* An independent check that protects customers and Harris' reputation as the network scales.
  

**This role is NOT:**

* The owner of plant production or shop-floor output (Manufacturing Operations).
* The owner of the Harris corporate QA/QC program.
* The owner of VDC's internal QA/QC (VDC).
* Responsible for safety programs or safety stop-work (Safety).
* The owner of product design or productization (Product Engineering).

Rezolute is a pre-commercial ultra-rare disease company focused on significantly improving outcomes for individuals with hypoglycemia caused by hyperinsulinism (HI). Our fully human monoclonal antibody therapy, RZ358 (ersodetug), is designed to treat all forms of HI and has shown substantial benefit in clinical trials and real-world use for the treatment of congenital hyperinsulinism (cHI) and tumor hyperinsulinism (tHI).

**Position Summary**

Rezolute is seeking a proactive, execution-focused project management professional to coordinate external manufacturing programs as the company advances toward commercial manufacturing.

The Senior Manager, Project Management - External Manufacturing will manage integrated plans, communications, and deliverables across technology transfer, GMP manufacturing, process characterization, process validation, and commercial readiness. Working with internal functional leads and contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs), this individual will align schedules, supplier commitments, and cross-functional dependencies with Rezolute’s Plan of Record (POR), supply requirements, and business priorities.

This role owns project coordination and follow-through, not technical oversight. External Manufacturing Operations, Manufacturing Science and Technology (MSAT), Quality Assurance (QA), and designated functional experts retain responsibility for technical strategy, scientific assessments, manufacturing process decisions, and quality approvals.

### **Principal Duties and Responsibilities**

Integrated Project Planning and Execution

* Develop and maintain integrated project plans for external Drug Substance (DS) and Drug Product (DP) programs, defining scope, deliverables, owners, milestones, dependencies, and target dates.

* Align project baselines and supplier commitments with the POR, supply requirements, and approved priorities.

* Monitor critical-path activities and progress against plan; coordinate recovery actions for overdue or at-risk commitments with functional owners and suppliers.

* Assess scope, schedule, and resource changes with accountable stakeholders and route proposed changes through established approval processes.

Communications and Cross-Functional Coordination

* Serve as the project management point of contact between Rezolute teams and CDMOs, facilitating cross-functional coordination and timely communication of changes.

* Lead internal and supplier project meetings, using focused agendas to address progress, upcoming deliverables, dependencies, and decisions required.

* Maintain and distribute meeting records and action items with clear owners and due dates; drive follow-through to closure.

Workstream and Milestone Coordination

* Coordinate manufacturing and milestone readiness by tracking prerequisites, including material availability, documentation, internal reviews, and supplier deliverables.

* Integrate technical and quality review timelines into project schedules, including protocols, reports, and master or electronic batch records.

* Track schedule dependencies associated with change controls, deviations, investigations, and other quality-system activities in partnership with QA and technical owners.

* Coordinate handoffs from development and validation activities to routine commercial manufacturing, tracking agreed deliverables, receiving owners, and outstanding actions.

Risk, Issue, and Decision Management

* Maintain risk, issue, assumption, decision, and dependency logs, including accountable owners and required completion dates.

* Work with functional leads and suppliers to assess execution risks and track mitigation actions and residual risks.

Reporting, Scope, and Project Controls

* Provide dashboards and leadership updates showing milestone performance, forecast completion dates, critical-path activities, risks, and decisions or intervention required.

* Partner with External Manufacturing leadership, Supplier Relationship Management (SRM), Business, and Procurement to define milestones, deliverables, assumptions, and timelines in supplier scopes of work.

* Support project-level financial tracking with budget owners, including planned work, supplier milestones, and the budget and schedule impacts of scope changes.

* Improve project management tools, reporting practices, and lessons-learned processes across the external manufacturing network.

* Experience coordinating technology transfer, GMP manufacturing, process characterization, process validation, or commercial manufacturing readiness activities.

existing_roles.description:
**About Marvell**

Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities.

At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead.

**Your Team, Your Impact**

Marvell's Connectivity firmware organization delivers firmware for our connectivity and optics product lines. This role owns the full Architecture & Quality function for that portfolio. Architecture and quality operate as one integrated group, a shared resource to every firmware team and not a gate in front of them.  
  
You will set the technical architecture direction for the portfolio and hold the quality bar across it, treating the two as a single end-to-end responsibility. Architecture shapes what can be verified, and quality is how we prove it, from requirements through release and into the field. You will be accountable for how architecture decisions are made, how firmware is verified and released, and how well the firmware, hardware and systems teams work together. You will lead a global team of senior technical leaders and are expected to build depth in a function that is currently concentrated in a few people.

**What You Can Expect**

This is one function, not two. Architecture decisions set what can be tested, and quality findings feed straight back into architecture. You will own the full lifecycle from requirements and design through verification, release and field support.

**Architecture that is built to be verified**

* Product and systems architecture across the Connectivity firmware portfolio: reference architectures, standards, design reviews and technical decision records, each with testability and observability designed in.
* Product hardware interlink: the architectural contract between hardware and firmware, covering requirements, interface definition, bring-up readiness and silicon-to-firmware feedback loops, with validation criteria agreed up front.
* CMIS and optics architecture: firmware architecture for CMIS-based modules and optics products, including spec compliance, feature roadmap and interoperability, tied directly to conformance and interop test plans.
* Architecture governance that scales: lightweight review processes, clear ownership and reusable components, so teams move faster instead of waiting on reviews.

**Quality as an end-to-end discipline**

* Quality strategy that starts at requirements and architecture review, not at test execution: shift-left practices, requirements quality and design-for-test standards owned jointly with the architects.
* Software Quality Assurance (SQA) strategy and execution: test strategy, automation, regression coverage, release qualification and defect trends.
* Release readiness and quality gates for all firmware releases, with clear exit criteria and a straight, data-backed go/no-go recommendation.
* Quality metrics and reporting to Engineering leadership, Product Management and customer-facing teams.

**Closing the loop**

* Customer-escape and defect analysis that traces root causes back to architecture, interfaces and process, and turns the learning into updated patterns, standards and test coverage.
* A single set of metrics and quality signals shared across architecture, interlink, optics and SQA, so design risk and test findings are managed in one view.

**Organization**

* Lead and develop a global organization (30+).
* Grow and retain senior technical talent, and manage the pipeline, hiring, succession and career paths for architects and quality engineers.
* Build a collaborative partnership with Firmware, Hardware, Systems, Product and Program Management, and with the Optics and telemetry teams.
* Own the function's budget, headcount plan, requisitions and tooling or lab investments.

**Your Team**

You will lead a small team of senior leaders and architects who together cover the function end to end, with architecture and quality responsibilities intentionally overlapping:

* Software quality assurance and release qualification.
* Hardware and firmware interlink.
* Optics and module architecture.
* Product and systems architecture.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Set a multi-year architecture and quality roadmap aligned with product and customer priorities, and drive it across engineering teams that do not report to you.
* Make and communicate hard trade-offs between schedule, scope and quality, and own the release recommendation.
* Raise the architecture bar: consistent patterns, reuse across product lines, and early detection of design risk before it becomes schedule risk.
* Shift quality left: embed test, automation and requirements quality earlier in the lifecycle, and invest in CI/CD, simulation, emulation and lab infrastructure.
* Represent Architecture & Quality in executive reviews and in technical engagements with key customers and standards bodies.
* Keep the function independent and credible: escalate quality risks directly and transparently, including when the news is unwelcome.
* Build the next layer of leadership so the function does not depend on any one person, and set clear delegation across the architecture and SQA leads.
* Manage a distributed team across time zones with clear rituals, ownership and handoffs.

**What We're Looking For**

* BS or MS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or a related field.
* 15+ years in embedded firmware or systems software for semiconductor, networking or optical products, including 8+ years leading managers or senior technical leaders.
* Track record owning both architecture and quality outcomes for shipping firmware products at scale.
* Deep working knowledge of firmware architecture for connectivity or optics products, with direct experience in HW/FW co-design and silicon bring-up.
* Hands-on experience with test strategy and automation, release qualification and quality metrics for complex, customer-deployed products.
* Experience leading globally distributed teams across multiple sites and cultures, including offshore QA/SQA organizations.
* Proven executive communication: able to present risk, trade-offs and recommendations to VP-level and customer audiences.

**Preferred Experience**

* Experience with CMIS and optical module firmware (for example 400G/800G and coherent or pluggable optics), and related industry standards and interoperability programs.
* Familiarity with Ethernet PHY, retimer, DSP or SerDes firmware, and with security features such as MACsec.
* Experience with secure firmware update, recovery and lifecycle practices.
* Background building or transforming an SQA organization, including automation and CI/CD maturity.
* Experience in a matrixed, platform-style organization where architecture is a shared service.

**Expected Base Pay Range (USD)**

218,850 - 327,800, $ per annum

The successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location and market conditions. The expected base pay range for this role may be modified based on market conditions.

This role is eligible to participate in Marvell's bonus and equity plans, including a new hire equity grant and annual equity refreshers, ensuring you are rewarded for your contributions and remain invested in the company's long-term success.

**Additional Compensation and Benefit Elements**

Marvell is committed to providing exceptional, comprehensive benefits that support our employees at every stage - from internship to retirement and through life’s most important moments. Our offerings are built around four key pillars: financial well-being, family support, mental and physical health, and recognition. Highlights include an employee stock purchase plan with a 2-year look back, family support programs to help balance work and home life, robust mental health resources to prioritize emotional well-being, and a recognition and service awards to celebrate contributions and milestones. We look forward to sharing more with you during the interview process.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status.

Any applicant who requires a reasonable accommodation during the selection process should contact Marvell HR Helpdesk at TAOps@marvell.com.

Translating customer feedback, field performance, warranty data, and quality insights into priorities that improve products, services, processes, and support. This leader provides oversight and direction for improving the customer experience and connects Design for Reliability, Supplier Quality Management, Manufacturing Process Control, field quality, and Customer Service & Support into an integrated end-to-end customer experience. Working closely with commercial, product, engineering, procurement, manufacturing, service, and regional leaders, this position drives rapid issue resolution, systemic corrective action, and continuous improvement across the full product life cycle to increase customer satisfaction, loyalty, and business performance.

* Own, create, and execute the enterprise-wide global customer experience and quality strategy, setting direction, priorities, and standards, and measurable objectives that advance business objectives, strengthens customer loyalty, and continuously improves customer outcomes.

* Develop, govern, and continuously improve an integrated enterprise performance system covering customer satisfaction, complaint responsiveness, repeat issues, field reliability, warranty, external PPM, first-pass yield, and cost of poor quality.

existing_roles.description:
Xona is the navigational intelligence company bringing real-time, centimeter-level certainty to any device, anywhere on Earth.

With Pulsar – the world’s most advanced PNT satellite infrastructure in Low Earth Orbit – Xona will offer a future-proof, backwards-compatible global positioning system optimized for absolute precision, superior power, and robust protection.

As production grows, we need clear evidence that each spacecraft meets its requirements and a quality system that helps teams find and resolve risks early.

We are looking for a **Senior Manager, Quality Operations** to lead US quality for satellite buses and payloads from incoming material through building, test and acceptance. You will build a pragmatic system and lead engineers and inspectors close to the floor. You have independent authority to hold work or withhold readiness concurrence and to escalate unresolved mission risk. This is a hands-on leadership role in a fast-moving, dynamic environment.

**What you will do:**
=====================

* Lead US quality engineers and inspectors across supplier, receiving, production and test coverage. Set training, inspection points and delegated authority.
* Own fit-for-stage quality controls for document and configuration records, serial and lot traceability, calibration, nonconformances, corrective action and acceptance packages.
* Define risk-based controls for critical characteristics and supplier parts. Work with Supply Chain on qualifications, escapes, containment and verified corrective action.
* Make quality status visible through yield, repeat defects, escapes, NCR aging and acceptance-record completeness. Use trends to improve controls with Manufacturing and Engineering.
* Own the quality hold and escalation process. Engineering owns technical disposition; Quality evaluates controls and evidence and concurs on release.
* Concur independently on quality evidence at acceptance and flight readiness reviews. Escalate residual risk despite schedule pressure; partner with Engineering on reliability and mission risk.
* Align common requirements with the Canada Quality Lead and feed ground defects and on-orbit anomalies into later builds.

**What we are looking for**
===========================

* 8+ years in quality engineering or quality management for aerospace, defense or similarly complex hardware, including 3+ years directly leading engineers, inspectors or specialists through production and test.
* Experience building a usable QMS and leading teams through supplier escapes, nonconformances, root cause and corrective action.
* Independent judgment, strong technical communication and the ability to separate Engineering disposition from Quality release concurrence.
* Working knowledge of configuration control, risk-based inspection, process capability and cross-functional investigations.
* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, materials science, physics or a related technical field, or equivalent quality leadership experience in complex hardware.

**For U.S. Roles:** To comply with U.S. Government space technology export regulations, applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the United States (i.e. Green Card holder), or other protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3).

**For U.K. Roles:** To comply with U.K. regulations, this role requires Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) checks, and successful candidates must be eligible to obtain UK Security Clearance (SC).

**For Canada Roles:** Successful candidates must obtain and hold a security clearance at the reliability status level, and pass security assessment for the Canadian Controlled Goods Program (CGP) and ITAR.

We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

Compensation Range: $180K - $230K

Stored Energy Systems (SENS) is an award-winning manufacturer of premium quality power conversion products located in Longmont, CO. **Summary**

SENS is seeking a manufacturing engineering leader to help build and scale the organization, processes, and technical capabilities required for our next stage of growth. Supporting the expansion of existing manufacturing operations and establishing new operations at our Broomfield Systems manufacturing factory, this leader will establish the manufacturing engineering strategy, develop a multidisciplinary team, and translate business growth plans into manufacturing capacity and reliable production processes for our fastest-growing products.

This role leads manufacturing engineering, industrialization, tooling, test systems, automation, and technical production support for our systems products, with a strong emphasis on configure-to-order assembly manufacturing. Working closely with Production, Design Engineering, Quality, Safety, and Supply Chain, the Senior Manager will establish clear priorities, strengthen new product and production transfer readiness, and deliver measurable improvements in productivity, quality, cost, and equipment reliability.

A successful candidate will combine organizational leadership with practical technical judgment, building a team that can support daily production while executing the improvements and investments needed to scale.

**Responsibilities**

* Help to build and develop the manufacturing engineering organization. Assess current capabilities, define the team structure and staffing plan, recruit talent, and develop engineers and technical leaders to support SENS’s growth.
* Establish performance measures and execution discipline. Set departmental goals, review project and operational performance, communicate risks and resource needs, and hold the team accountable for measurable improvements in manufacturing readiness, capacity, productivity, and equipment reliability.
* Establish and execute the manufacturing engineering roadmap. Translate business growth, product plans, and production requirements into prioritized initiatives for manufacturing capacity, processes, tooling, test systems, automation, and equipment reliability.
* Lead manufacturing readiness for new products and production transfers. Partner with Design Engineering, Production, Quality, and Planning & Fulfillment to establish readiness criteria and ensure processes, equipment, tooling, test capability, documentation, and training are in place before production release.
* Develop scalable manufacturing processes and standards. Establish consistent methods for process development, validation, work instructions, engineering changes, and production controls across manufacturing locations while accommodating product-specific requirements.
* Expand manufacturing capacity and improve productivity. Lead engineering efforts in capacity analysis, line balancing, factory layout, workflow, cycle-time reduction, and constraint elimination to support production demand and improve labor efficiency.
* Provide reliable technical support to Production. Establish clear support coverage, escalation processes, and problem-solving practices that resolve production issues promptly and prevent recurrence while maintaining progress on strategic projects.
* Guide manufacturing technology development. Lead technical specialists responsible for manufacturing test systems, production software, tooling, and automation. Prioritize investments based on safety, quality, capacity, reliability, and financial return.
* Improve production equipment reliability. Establish equipment ownership, maintenance strategies, critical spare requirements, and preventive and predictive maintenance practices in partnership with Production and technical support teams.
* Manage projects, capital investments, and departmental resources. Develop business cases, budgets, schedules, and resource plans; oversee implementation and production acceptance; and verify that projects deliver their expected operational and financial benefits.
* Partner with Design Engineering on manufacturability. Incorporate manufacturing feedback early in product development and engineering changes to improve assembly, testability, quality, serviceability, and cost.
* Drive safe processes and sustained quality improvement. Partner with EHS and Quality to incorporate risk assessment, error prevention, root cause analysis, and corrective action into manufacturing processes and equipment changes.
* Oversee the development and maintenance of manufacturing processes, work instructions, test procedures, tooling, fixtures, automation systems, and production software solutions.
* Be directly accountable for engineering project delivery, manufacturing readiness, equipment reliability, and validated improvement benefits, while sharing accountability with Production and Quality for labor efficiency and first-pass yield (FPY).

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline, or an additional 4 years of manufacturing engineering experience.
* Eight or more years of experience in manufacturing engineering, production engineering, industrialization, or a related technical manufacturing role.
* Three or more years of experience directly leading engineering or technical teams, including setting priorities, developing employees, allocating resources, and managing performance.
* Demonstrated success improving manufacturing performance, with measurable results in productivity, capacity, quality, cost, or equipment reliability.
* Experience developing and improving manufacturing processes, tooling, fixtures, work instructions, and production controls, including introducing new or revised products into production.

* Experience leading cross-functional projects with Production, Design Engineering, Quality, Safety, and Supply Chain, balancing daily production needs with longer-term improvement priorities.
* Experience planning and executing manufacturing improvement or capital equipment projects, including defining scope, schedules, resource requirements, and expected business results.
* Strong communication and organizational skills, with the ability to translate business objectives into clear team priorities and communicate progress, risks, and decisions.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in manufacturing of configure-to-order (CTO) and engineered-to-order (ETO) electrical systems such as switchgear, switchboard, etc.
* Experience with manufacturing software development, automated test systems, and data acquisition platforms.
* Experience using ERP systems such as SyteLine for BOM management, item masters, engineering changes, and manufacturing planning.
* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt, Black Belt, or equivalent certification.
* Experience managing departmental budgets and capital equipment projects from business case through production acceptance.
