existing_roles.description:
**Be one of the Bedo 100**
--------------------------

Albedo is making Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) mainstream, building the infrastructure to enable every satellite mission to enter this new orbital domain. We build buses, integrated satellites, and turnkey missions for customers to thrive in VLEO, below 300 km, where proximity compounds performance and drag self-cleans debris.

As part of the first 100 employees at Albedo, you will have a big impact on Albedo's trajectory to proliferating VLEO — whether you're advancing hardware to increase satellite longevity, scaling production for large constellations, building next-gen flight and ground software to push performance, or enabling missions that matter for national security and our day-to-day life here on Earth.

**How We Operate:** Albedo takes a first-principles approach — in space and in business. We move with speed, take calculated risks, and learn quickly. We use AI regularly to create leverage in every discipline across the company. We work in-person at our Broomfield, CO HQ to maximize team and company productivity. We work hard and with urgency to compound our first-mover advantage.

**Who We're Looking For:** Builders who want to own outcomes, not tasks. Systems thinkers who balance precision with iteration while thinking about the big picture. Individuals who are energized by creating a category rather than competing in an existing one. You'll join a team that has already proven what others said wasn't feasible and is now scaling and upgrading our VLEO buses & payloads to serve mission sets across sensing, communications, and responsive operations.

If you can feel the excitement running through your veins, apply to be one of the Bedo 100.

### **What You'll Do:**

* Own Albedo's production operations across Supply Chain, Assembly, Integration & Test (AI&T), and Facilities, ensuring flight hardware is delivered on schedule, within budget, and to quality requirements.
* Lead and develop a multidisciplinary team of engineers, technicians, test personnel, and supply chain professionals, including hiring, performance management, and workforce planning.
* Develop and execute integrated production plans, aligning material readiness, build schedules, staffing, and test capacity across vehicle and subsystem builds.
* Set supply chain strategy and priorities, ensuring sourcing, supplier development, procurement, and long-lead planning stay ahead of production demand.
* Oversee AI&T execution from assembly through integration, functional and environmental testing, and delivery. Drive improvements in processes, tooling, and test infrastructure.
* Lead facilities and production infrastructure planning, including buildout, commissioning, equipment, capacity expansion, and EHS.
* Establish and track operational metrics, including supplier delivery, material readiness, schedule adherence, labor efficiency, throughput, and first-pass yield.
* Partner with Engineering, Quality, Program Management, and Finance to transition designs into production, resolve risks, and align resources and priorities.
* Identify and prioritize improvements to production processes, tooling, and systems, balancing cost, schedule, and scalability.
* Lead major operational initiatives, including production rate increases, facility stand-up, and ERP/MES implementations.
* Remove roadblocks, support hands-on problem-solving, and champion a culture of safety, quality, accountability, and continuous improvement.

### **Your Ideal Skills and Experience:**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Operations, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* 8–12+ years of experience in aerospace or complex hardware manufacturing, spanning production, AI&T, and supply chain, with 5+ years leading technical teams.
* Proven ability to build and manage multidisciplinary teams, including hiring, workforce planning, performance management, and employee development.
* Strong understanding of spacecraft or similarly complex hardware assembly, integration, and test, including mechanical, electrical, functional, and environmental testing.
* Working knowledge of demand planning, MRP, strategic sourcing, supplier management, and long-lead procurement.
* Experience scaling manufacturing operations and facilities, including equipment, tooling, capacity planning, and EHS.
* Ability to balance cost, schedule, quality, and technical risk while identifying constraints and driving operational improvements.
* Experience managing operational KPIs, with familiarity in ERP/MRP, MES, QMS, configuration management, and aerospace workmanship standards.
* Strong leadership and communication skills, with a hands-on, solutions-oriented approach suited to a fast-paced startup environment.

### **Salary Range:**

* $168,197 - $190,000 per year

#### **Compensation and Benefits for Full-Time Roles:**

* + Employee friendly equity compensation
  + 4% direct matching 401k
  + Health Insurance: 100% employee coverage & 75% dependent coverage
  + Parental leave and childcare coverage
  + Flexible vacation and sick time from day one
  + 12 company holidays
  + $100 monthly wellness benefit
  + Relocation package if not based in Denver

*The final compensation package is subject to change if the candidate's experience and company need drive a different job level than originally slated for the position.*

*Albedo does not accept agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to Albedo employees. Albedo is not responsible for any fees or overhead related to unsolicited resumes.*

**AI Disclosure:** We may use Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology to support and enhance our recruitment process. This includes recording, transcribing, analyzing, and evaluating your interview responses to ensure accurate, consistent, and efficient assessment of job-related skills, knowledge, and abilities. While AI tools may assist in this process, our human recruiting and hiring teams make all hiring decisions. For questions about AI use in interviews, data handling, or to request accommodations, contact Hello\_HR@albedo.com

  

**Additional Requirements:** In compliance with federal law, all persons hired must verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and complete the required employment eligibility verification form upon hire. All persons hired will be required to be a U.S. citizen, a lawful permanent resident of the U.S., or a protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

**Equal Opportunity Employer/Veterans/Disabled:** Albedo is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

**Relocation:** Relocation support for this position is available

Applicants must be a **U.S. Person** as defined under 22 CFR 120.62

#LI-Onsite

*Research shows that while men apply to jobs where they meet an average of 60% of the criteria, women and other underrepresented people tend to only apply when they meet 100% of the qualifications. At Albedo, we'd rather hear from you. We care more about how you think than which boxes you check. We value people who do the math, make their assumptions explicit, and ask the annoying questions: what breaks, what's the failure mode, what has to be true for this to work? If that sounds like you, apply, even if you don't meet every line.*

**Overview**
Resonetics is a global leader in advanced engineering, prototyping, product development, and micro manufacturing, driving innovation in the medical device industry. With rapid expansion across all our locations, we continue to push the boundaries of technology while fostering a dynamic, employee-centered culture. Our commitment to excellence and continuous improvement makes Resonetics an exciting place for professionals passionate about shaping the future of micro-manufacturing and being part of something bigger
  
  
The Quality Director plays a pivotal role in leading and strengthening operational quality and quality compliance within a large-scale contract manufacturing facility. Responsible for both Product Quality and Quality Management System (QMS) compliance, this leader ensures quality operations within the manufacturing environment consistently meet customer, regulatory, and business expectations.
  
  
This individual combines strategic vision with hands-on operational quality leadership, ensuring Resonetics delivers world-class quality in a fast-paced, highly regulated medical device manufacturing environment. The role demands proven experience within manufacturing operations, deep expertise in ISO 13485 and 21 CFR Part 820, mastery of advanced quality assurance techniques, and the ability to align and elevate quality performance across multiple value streams.
  
  
Join Resonetics and be part of a team that’s redefining medical device manufacturing. If you’re passionate about innovation and thrive in a fast-paced environment, we’d love to hear from you.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
**Operational Quality Leadership**

* Own and lead all aspects of manufacturing quality performance, ensuring operational processes deliver consistent, compliant, and high-yield outcomes.
* Partner closely with Operations leadership to embed quality into daily production activities and drive problem-solving directly on the manufacturing floor.
* Implement and oversee statistical process control (SPC), process capability, and other data-driven tools to ensure process stability and continuous improvement.
* Monitor and manage critical quality metrics, taking immediate action to address gaps and prevent recurrence of issues.
* Oversee validation strategies (IQ/OQ/PQ) for manufacturing processes and equipment, ensuring robustness and compliance.
* Provide quality leadership in New Product Introduction (NPI), ensuring robust process validation, risk management, and seamless transition from development into full-scale manufacturing.

**Quality Systems & Compliance**

* Ensure the ISO-certified QMS is operationally effective within manufacturing sites and continuously improved to support business growth.
* Maintain full compliance with ISO 13485, 21 CFR Part 820, and other relevant standards through proactive system management and audit readiness.

**Continuous Improvement & Problem Solving**

* Lead root cause investigations and corrective actions for complex production challenges.
* Drive Lean and Six Sigma initiatives that enhance manufacturing efficiency while strengthening compliance and product quality.
* Share best practices across sites to ensure standardization and scalability of quality improvements.

**Customer & Supplier Interface**

* Serve as the primary quality leader for high-visibility customers, ensuring confidence in Resonetics’ ability to deliver consistently high-quality products.
* Lead the supplier quality program, ensuring raw materials and outsourced processes meet stringent requirements to support operational excellence.

**Team Leadership & Development**

* Build and mentor a strong quality team embedded within the manufacturing organization.
* Provide training in advanced quality tools (Gage R&R, SPC, pFMEA, Risk Analysis, Validation, Root Cause Analysis, CAPA) to elevate operational capability.
* Foster a culture of quality culture and ownership on the production floor, engaging all levels of the workforce.

**Required Qualifications**

* Minimum 7 years’ experience in a Medical Device Quality Management role.
* Lean and/or Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt
* Demonstrated background in an ISO 13485 and 21 CFR 820 quality management system.
* Strong communication skills (verbal and writing)
* BS degree in a management or engineering discipline
* Experience hosting FDA inspections and ISO audits

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Prior experience in a technical, regulated environment.
* Experience with finished medical device assembly and oversight of sterilization
* Experience with Quality Management Software (eQMS) and ERP systems
* Certified Quality Auditor

**Physical Demands**

* Light office work, approximately 25%+ travel

**Compensation**
The compensation for this role is competitive and will be based on experience and qualifications. The anticipated range is $144,000.00 - $222,000.00.
  
  
For temp, temp-to-hire, and regular full-time positions, our company policy is that we are unable to provide visa sponsorship. Candidates must already be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship now or in the future.

protected_roles.description:
**Position Summary**
The Director, Quality is responsible for leading multiple manufacturing/service sites and/or corporate quality resources in the execution of the overall STERIS Quality System. This position is principally responsible for manufacturing/service site or functional quality system execution to drive product/service quality improvement and ensure compliance with, as appropriate, ISO 9001, ISO 13485, MDSAP, FDA QMSR CFR Part 820/211, EU MDR, and other applicable standards. Supporting the GI Reprocessing business, this role provides quality leadership for products, processes, and services that help healthcare providers safely clean, disinfect, and reprocess gastrointestinal endoscopes and related equipment. The Director will champion a culture of quality, compliance, and continuous improvement, helping ensure the delivery of safe, effective, and reliable solutions that support infection prevention, patient safety, and customer confidence. The Quality Director will lead teams of quality managers and engineers responsible for product and service quality, supplier quality, new product/service support, continuous improvement initiatives, and quality system execution. This leader will partner closely with Operations, Engineering, Regulatory Affairs, and Commercial teams to drive operational excellence, mitigate risk, support innovation, and enhance quality performance across the GI Reprocessing portfolio.
  
  
Preferred onsite location: Mentor, OH, with consideration for candidates based in Plymouth, MN or Conroe, TX.
  
  
**What You’ll Do As a Director Quality**

* The Director, Quality will have responsibility for the following: Leads manufacturing/service sites and/or corporate quality staff in the execution and continuous improvement of the STERIS Quality System. Operates with a focus on the following objectives:

+ Ensures site level compliance to appropriate ISO, FDA, and other applicable regulatory standards.
+ Drives strategies and methods to continuously improve capital, consumable and service product quality performance.
+ Establishes clear and consistent quality measurement systems in order to monitor and drive results.
+ Leads quality planning and the execution of assigned New Product/Service Development (NPD) projects to achieve targeted quality deliverable adherence.
+ Drives targeted supplier quality improvement efforts and oversees supplier evaluation, approval, and control for assigned manufacturing sites.
+ Assists in the continuous improvement and standardization of quality system procedures and monitor effectiveness.
+ Supports the reliability function by integrating design for reliability tools and techniques within the local projects.
+ Leads quality planning efforts through cross-functional teaming at a site level.

* Supports the New Product/Service Development process and projects to ensure projects attain cost, quality, and delivery objectives.
* Directs local staff on planning sequential and concurrent quality activities. Establish planning and monitoring tools and techniques.
* Provides Quality viewpoints and opinions in planning and specifying existing and future products.
* Assists in the development of the Quality budget. Helps to ensures resources are adequate to fully support the Quality System.
* Takes ownership of all local quality issues, projects, and development activities. Works closely with the site’s Senior Management Teams to provide strategic direction and development of the manufacturing sites product quality strategies and tactics.
* Manages and provide direction to a teams of quality professionals both at corporate and manufacturing sites, with responsibility for hiring, performance management, appropriate staffing, and deployment of resources.
* Assures that local sites maintain and improve operational and quality systems to remain in a state of compliance to appropriate ISO, FDA, and other applicable regulatory standards.
* Works closely with the regulatory function to ensure compliance to appropriate ISO and FDA standards; plans for and assists in the management of external audits.
* Leads manufacturing and service site quality teams to ensure alignment to operations, support of Lean efforts and drive quality improvement performance for products, services, and processes across the sites.
* This individual has autonomy to perform the duties of Person Responsible for Regulatory Compliance (PRRC) on behalf of STERIS legal manufacturing entities under the EU MDR. This individual shall suffer no disadvantage within the organization in relation to proper fulfilment of his or her duties in lieu of article 15 of the EU MDR.

**Required**
**The Experience, Skills, and Abilities Needed**

* Bachelor’s Degree (Engineering or related technical field)
* Minimum 10 years of experience with increased responsibility leading quality system and product quality improvement efforts. Exceptional leadership manifested through organizing and motivating teams toward their respective goals by employing hands-on management.
* Must fulfil the experience requirements listed in Article 15 of the EUMDR (PRRC).
* A solid quality foundation indicated by a demonstrated understanding of Lean/Six Sigma, quality system, and product/process improvement methodologies.
* Solid business acumen and proven ability to build and lead process and product improvement strategies and results.

The Global Director of Quality is responsible for oversight of Quality Management and Continuous Improvement Programs for Team Industrial Services globally. Position is responsible for managing and coordinating all Quality support activities relating to the execution of the Quality Management System (QMS) for Team Corporate, Product and Service Line, Engineering and Manufacturing, and Operations. Global Director of Quality is responsible for operating on a cost-effective basis within the framework of company approved policies, objectives, and budgets.
  
  
**Essential Job Functions**

* Maintains a safe, secure and healthy environment by adhering to Company/Customer safety and quality standards and practices and to legal regulations, alerting others regarding potential hazards or concern
* Adheres to and is a champion of TEAM’s Core Values
* Establish a continuous improvement culture across the enterprise utilizing known methods and concepts such as Lean, Six Sigma, FMEA, Kaizen, Poka-yoke, CAPA, 8D, etc.
* Maintains contact with district, division and corporate levels to promote and instill a “Quality Culture” throughout the organization.
* Ensure TEAMs QMS is globally consistent and regionally precise based on local requirements.

* Experience with problem solving methods such as A3, FMEA, etc. preferred.

**Title: Director, Manufacturing Operations**
**Location: Kansas City, MO**
**Summary**
The Director, Manufacturing Operations provides leadership, direction, and oversight for manufacturing operations at the Kansas City site. The role is accountable for the safe, compliant, efficient, and customer-focused execution of clinical and commercial manufacturing programs while meeting business objectives for employee engagement, quality, delivery, and cost.
  
  
As a member of the Site Leadership Team, the Director, Manufacturing Operations partners across functions to develop and execute site strategy, support business growth, and continuously improve operational performance. The Director establishes a culture of safety, quality, accountability, inclusion, continuous improvement, and employee development.
  
  
**The Role**

* Provide strategic leadership and oversight of manufacturing operations supporting both clinical and commercial programs.
* Ensure safe, compliant, efficient execution of manufacturing activities while meeting customer expectations.
* Lead capacity planning, resource allocation, project onboarding, and operational readiness to support current and future business demand.
* Drive operational performance by prioritizing resources and achieving targets for quality, delivery, productivity, cycle time, and cost.
* Champion a strong culture of safety, GMP compliance, and regulatory readiness across all manufacturing activities.
* Partner with Quality and cross-functional teams to address investigations, deviations, CAPAs, audits, inspections, and compliance matters.
* Own manufacturing metrics, forecasting, budgeting, and financial performance, including operating and capital expenditure planning.
* Identify, justify, and implement operational and capital improvement initiatives that enhance safety, quality, efficiency, capacity, and profitability.
* Foster a culture of Lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, data-driven decision making, and operational excellence.
* Build and develop a high-performing organization through talent acquisition, coaching, succession planning, employee engagement, and inclusive leadership while contributing to overall site strategy and stakeholder relationships.

**The Candidate**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Business, or a related field required; advanced degree preferred.
* Minimum 12 years of experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, CDMO, or other highly regulated manufacturing environments.
* At least 7 years of manufacturing leadership experience, including leading managers and developing high-performing teams.
* Proven success supporting regulatory inspections, client audits, customer interactions, and pharmaceutical quality systems.
* Strong knowledge of GMP regulations, pharmaceutical manufacturing operations, and Quality-Operations partnerships; oral solid dosage experience preferred.
* Demonstrated business and financial acumen with the ability to balance quality, customer, operational, people, and financial priorities.
* Expertise in Lean manufacturing, operational excellence, continuous improvement, and data-driven problem solving.
* Excellent communication, presentation, client-service, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
* Strategic and change-oriented leader with the ability to translate business goals into operational priorities while driving organizational alignment and transformation.
* Strong talent development, decision-making, and leadership capabilities, with a track record of building succession pipelines, coaching leaders, influencing stakeholders, and representing the organization with employees, customers, regulators, and senior executives.

Please review the job details below.
  
  
Intuitive Machines - West is currently seeking a courageous, innovative, multi-skilled Director of High-Rate AIT Production to join our spacecraft production team in Palo Alto, CA.
  
  
**Life with Us**
Your Project: Intuitive Machines is a world leader in high-power spacecraft, having delivered some of the largest and highest-power spacecraft in the world. We are now looking to take this legacy of excellence to the next level, architecting a high-volume production line to build a large number of advanced spacecraft.
  
  
In this role, you will architect and implement a high-volume assembly, integration, and test (AIT) production line for these next-generation vehicles. You will be responsible for transforming our AIT operations from low-rate to high-rate production, establishing scalable processes and organizational capabilities to support our ambitious production targets. The scope includes complete spacecraft AIT from component receipt through final acceptance testing, encompassing electrical systems integration, solar array integration with the spacecraft bus, battery integration, advanced thermal solutions, and comprehensive environmental testing at production scale.
  
  
A critical aspect of this role is developing an efficient, right-sized test program—one that provides high confidence the vehicles will perform as designed while eliminating non-value-added test activities that add cost and schedule without commensurate risk reduction. You will apply rigorous engineering judgment to distinguish between essential verification activities and legacy testing practices that may not be necessary for production-rate vehicles.
  
  
We are looking for leaders to bravely challenge conventional AIT approaches and establish production-rate processes for these advanced systems. You will play an essential role in applying design-for-manufacturing/design-for-test (DFM/DFT) principles to develop AIT specifications and manufacturing plans suitable for volume production. Additionally, you will represent AIT capabilities during customer proposal efforts, providing technical credibility and instilling confidence in our ability to execute high-volume production of complex spacecraft.
  
  
Your Career: We're very serious about professional development and continuing education at Intuitive Machines - West. We offer our team members the opportunity to define their own career trajectory. You will work with your manager to set goals and design a development plan to advance your career. This unique opportunity is a high-visibility role critical to our company's leadership position in spacecraft manufacturing.
  
  
What We Offer: Time for dedicated professional development, conference attendance, industry training, peer group collaboration, as well as paid certifications and education reimbursement.
  
  
Who you will work with: You will report to the VP of Spacecraft Production and Operations and collaborate closely with Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain teams. You will lead a team of AIT production engineers and technicians while partnering with design engineering to ensure producibility of our spacecraft systems. You will also engage directly with potential customers during proposal phases to communicate our production and test capabilities.
  
  
**Your Responsibilities**

* Design end-to-end AIT production flow optimized for high-volume throughput
* Develop capacity models, takt time analysis, and process flow requirements for production-rate AIT
* Define capital equipment strategy including test equipment, handling systems, and tooling
* Establish scalable AIT work instructions, process controls, and quality gates
* Lead development of an efficient, risk-informed test program that ensures vehicle performance confidence while eliminating non-value-added testing
* Oversee spacecraft-level integration of solar arrays, batteries, and other major subsystems with the spacecraft bus
* Implement manufacturing execution systems (MES) tailored to provide assembly process documentation and production tracking for volume spacecraft production
* Define requirements for low-cost mechanical and electrical assembly, integration and test equipment, and production tooling
* Lead Voice of Manufacturing inputs to spacecraft design to ensure producibility at scale
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives leveraging lean manufacturing principles
* Build and mentor AIT production engineering team
* Represent AIT production capabilities to potential customers during proposal efforts, providing technical credibility on execution readiness
* Support business development with AIT cost models and production capacity commitments

**How You Will Be Evaluated**
Your performance will be measured against AIT production readiness milestones, test program efficiency metrics, production ramp targets, quality metrics, and cost per unit objectives.
  
  
**What We Look For In Team Members**
As a team member at Intuitive Machines - West, we expect you to demonstrate honesty, integrity, innovation, collaboration, and a commitment to excellence.
  
  
**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering or related technical field. Four additional years of experience may be substituted for a degree
* Minimum of 15 years related aerospace manufacturing/AIT experience
* Minimum of 7 years leadership experience in production or manufacturing engineering
* Experience working cross-functionally within a company and/or with external partners and contractors
* Proven track record scaling aerospace production operations
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with volume production of spacecraft or complex aerospace systems
* Direct experience developing and implementing a spacecraft AIT production line
* Experience with large spacecraft systems (solar array integration, battery integration, high-voltage testing)
* Demonstrated experience developing efficient, risk-based test programs that balance verification rigor with schedule/cost efficiency
* Understanding of spacecraft environmental testing at production scale (thermal vacuum, vibration, EMI/EMC)
* Prior history as an AIT engineer, process engineer, or industrial engineer for aerospace products
* Experience with sustaining engineering processes such as Change Approval, NPI, breakpointing
* Advanced degree in a technical field
* Lean/Six Sigma certification
* Experience with AS9100 quality systems
* Capital project management experience (multi-million dollar equipment investments)
* Experience taking spacecraft products into production, including progressive design iterations to reduce delivered cost
* Demonstrated experience applying system engineering practices to AIT operations
* Excellent communication and presentation skills, with experience engaging directly with customers in technical/proposal settings
* Experience working directly with customers in the commercial space industry
* Ability to work independently with a high degree of organization and attention to detail

***Why Valmont***
**We’re Here to Move the World Forward.**
Valmont impacts millions of people around the world every day, yet they might not realize the many ways. Our technology is helping feed the growing population, supplying the world with more reliable energy and access to renewables, enhancing connectivity in remote and urban locations to create a sustainable future and so much more. 1000 company that respects hard work, honors diversity and invests in our employees as we focus on creating the world of tomorrow, today.
*We are the modern workforce*
. Are you ready to move the world forward? Apply now.
  
  
**A Brief Summary Of This Position**
The Plant Manager is accountable for end-to-end operations of the Elkhart plant and for achieving Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost (SQDC) objectives. The incumbent provides leadership, direction, planning, and control across manufacturing, materials/purchasing, production scheduling, and shipping to ensure products are produced safely, meet customer and regulatory requirements, and are delivered complete and on time. This role drives continuous improvement and operational excellence, develops and coaches leaders, and manages budgets and cost controls to optimize productivity, quality performance, and overall plant profitability.
  
  
**Essential Functions**

* Ensure that all administrative, supervisory and hourly positions are staffed with the best qualified personnel available.
* Drive team engagement through regular coaching, feedback and involvement in day-to-day operations.
* Foster an environment of open communication.
* Maintain required professional competencies; assess staffing levels and capability; and develop direct reports through training and development opportunities.
* Empower all employees to seek and recommend work methods, tools and procedures to improve safety, quality, delivery and cost functions.
* Develop, coach, and hold leaders and teams accountable through clear expectations, training, and performance management.
* Enforce company policies and procedures in partnership with HR, the Site Controller and operational leadership.
* Lead and sustain a continuous improvement culture across all departments.
* Own site performance to Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost (SQDC) targets by setting expectations, reviewing results, and driving corrective actions with the Production and Materials team, including:

+ Safety: OSHA recordable incident rate (TRIR) and VSI leading indicators
+ Quality: CoPQ: Internal (scrap and rework) and External (customer defects/complaints)
+ Delivery: SCOT (Ship Complete On Time)
+ Cost: labor and overhead (burden) performance vs. budget/standard
+ Cost: operating profit / plant financial performance
+ Cost/Working Capital: inventory turns and inventory accuracy
+ Cost: manufacturing expense per earned hour / pcs (TME)

* Ensure equipment, processes, and behaviors comply with safety requirements.
* Maintain product quality standards and lead ongoing continuous improvement efforts related to quality.
* Ensure that production and shipment of product meets or exceeds the conformance and delivery expectations of product users and customers.
* Lead cross-functional alignment across sales/marketing, engineering, manufacturing, production control, and off-site operations to achieve SQDC commitments.
* Review daily/weekly SQDC performance and implement countermeasures to protect on-time shipment and cost targets.
* Communicate plant priorities, performance, and changes to hourly and salaried employees.
* Manage inventory to support SCOT while minimizing working capital and obsolescence.
* Oversee preventative maintenance systems in an effort to maintain and protect physical corporate assets.
* Ensure strong systems are in place and functioning to drive asset reliability.
* Lead site-level control activities by communicating expectations and ensuring alignment through a strong partnership with the site Controller.
* Recommend improvements to controls, monitor compliance, and provide accountability to senior management.

**Required Qualifications of Every Candidate (Education, Experience, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities):**

* Preferred Bachelors with 7+ years relevant experience or Associates Degree with 9+ years relevant experience or 11+ years of relevant experience
* Seven or more years of progressive management experience in a manufacturing environment
* Extensive experience with budget and cost management
* Working knowledge of all areas of production from material procurement, transformation, through to shipment
* Experience using MS Office (PowerPoint, Word, Excel, Outlook)
* Ability to travel up to 10%, including overnights

**Highly Qualified Candidates Will Also Possess These Qualifications**

* B.S. in Manufacturing, Business, Technology, or related field is preferred
* Master’s Degree
* Prior experience as a Plant Manager of a manufacturing facility

**Working Environment And Physical Efforts**
Work is typically performed in a manufacturing plant environment and the incumbent needs to be able to move about the office and production environments. There is often exposure to conditions such as dust, dirt, heat, fumes, and cold as well as noise levels above 80 decibels. Many aspects of this role are physical and the incumbent has to be able to lift up to 50 lbs. The employee is regularly required to reach with hands and arms. The incumbent is frequently required to stand, walk, sit, use hands to finger, handle, feel, as well as balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, talk, and hear. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, and depth perception.
  
  
**Benefits**
Valmont offers employees and their families a comprehensive Total Wellbeing benefit package to ensure their individual and family’s overall wellness needs are met. Some offerings are dependent upon the role, work schedule, or location and can include the following:
  
  

* Healthcare (medical, prescription drugs, dental and vision)
* 401k retirement plan with company match
* Paid time off
* Employer paid life insurance
* Employer paid short-term and long-term disability including maternity leave
* Work Life Support
* Tuition Reimbursement up to $5,250 per year
* Voluntary programs like tobacco cessation, Type 2 diabetes reversal, one-on-one health coaching, mortgage services and more

Valmont does not discriminate against any employee or applicant in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, genetic information, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by law. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
  
  
If you have a disability and require any assistance in filling out the application for employment email EEOCompliance@Valmont.com.

**Job Description**
The Director PMO NPI/NPD is responsible for leading the successful transition of new products from R&D into scalable volume manufacturing. Sitting within the PMO and reporting to the VP of Production Engineering and Continuous Improvement (PECI), this role owns NPI execution, manufacturing readiness, and phase-gate milestone delivery across the product portfolio. The Director partners closely with Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, and Product Management to ensure products transition seamlessly into volume manufacturing — meeting customer, quality, cost, and delivery expectations — while building the processes, tooling, and team capabilities needed to scale.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**
**New Product Development & Launch**

* Own PLM milestone tracking, phase-gate execution, and portfolio pipeline alignment to ensure timely and effective product launches
* Drive product commercialization from R&D handoff through launch, ensuring new products meet or exceed customer, quality, cost, and delivery requirements
* Align cross-functionally on the new product pipeline and launch readiness across Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, and Product Management

**Manufacturing Readiness & Scale-Up**

* Lead the transition of products from R&D into volume manufacturing, establishing scalable and repeatable production processes
* Develop and ramp manufacturing capability and capacity for new products at the R&D site
* Establish and continuously improve the R&D production line to support prototype and pilot builds

**Automation, Tooling & Test**

* Lead automation initiatives including tooling, test fixtures, and production test requirement definition
* Partner with Engineering and Operations to ensure test and tooling solutions are scalable for volume production

**Team Leadership**

* Lead and develop a team of Technical Program Managers and the Engineering Manager for Prototype and Pilot Builds
* Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement within the NPD PMO function

**Skill & Abilities**
**Ownership & Accountability**
Ability to drive NPI program outcomes from R&D handoff through volume manufacturing launch. Holds themselves and their team to commitments, drives decisions, and escalates risks proactively — ensuring programs stay on track.
  
  
**Program & Portfolio Management**
Ability to manage multiple NPI programs simultaneously across the portfolio, maintaining phase-gate discipline, milestone ownership, and pipeline visibility from commercialization through volume launch.
  
  
**Commercialization & NPI Execution**
Ability to take products through the commercialization phase — from R&D handoff to volume manufacturing — on time and within cost, quality, and delivery targets.
  
  
**Manufacturing & Production Readiness**
Deep understanding of manufacturing processes, scale-up requirements, tooling, automation, and test development — with the ability to translate R&D outputs into production-ready solutions.
  
  
**Cross-Functional Leadership & Influence**
Ability to align and drive execution across Engineering, Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, and Product Management without direct authority over all stakeholders — critical in a PMO structure.
  
  
**Strategic Thinking & Prioritization**
Ability to manage competing program priorities at the portfolio level, make sound trade-off decisions, and keep initiatives aligned to business objectives.
  
  
**Team Development**
Ability to lead, develop and effectively scale a team to ensure the right capabilities and resourcing are in place at the right time.
  
  
**Stakeholder Communication & Reporting**
Ability to synthesize program status, risks, and decisions into clear, concise communication for senior leadership and the c-suite.
  
  
**Travel**
Ability to travel 10-20%
  
  
**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a related technical field
* 15+ years of program management experience in a manufacturing or engineering environment, with a focus on new product introduction (NPI), product transitions, or manufacturing scale-up
* 5+ years of team leadership/management role within a PMO, R&D, or Operations function

Chefman is one of North America's leading brands of small kitchen appliances, committed to building best-in-class products that make cooking accessible and enjoyable. This is not a desk job. We need a leader who has personally run a factory floor, someone who can walk into an assembly line, spot a process problem before it becomes a quality escape, and work directly with factory teams to fix it. You'll serve as the critical bridge between our design and product development teams here in Mahwah and our manufacturing partners in China, helping ensure that what we design translates seamlessly into what gets built at scale.
  
  
We're looking for a leader with deep, sustained manufacturing expertise, ideally 10 to 15 years building that expertise with one organization, who is ready to bring that experience to a fast-growing, entrepreneurial consumer brand. This role requires extensive travel to China and a genuine passion for being present where products come to life.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead manufacturing strategy and execution across our overseas partner network, from tooling and assembly process design through high-volume mass production
* Partner early and often with Product Development and Industrial Design teams, bringing manufacturing expertise directly into design decisions to support manufacturability, cost efficiency, and quality from day one

* Build and maintain rigorous reporting and documentation systems that give leadership clear visibility into yield, quality performance, and production trends across all partner sites
* Lead structured root-cause investigations (8D, 5-Why, Fishbone) when quality or performance opportunities arise, partnering closely with factory teams to implement durable, lasting solutions
* Serve as the senior point of contact for resolving complex production challenges, balancing quality, cost, and delivery priorities
* Build and develop a team of manufacturing and quality engineers to support the company's growing production needs
* Evaluate and help develop new manufacturing partnerships and capacity as the business scales
* Own the manufacturing cost and efficiency relationship, driving continuous improvement in profitability alongside quality

**Qualifications**

* 10-15+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, ideally with significant tenure at a single organization producing consumer electronics, small appliances, or similar consumer hardware products

* Deep, working-level understanding of injection molding, sheet metal, electromechanical assembly, and tooling processes, built through genuine hands-on experience
* Strong background in structured root-cause problem solving and driving continuous improvement initiatives with manufacturing partners
* Experience developing and aligning SOPs and best practices across multiple factory sites
* A natural inclination to stay close to product design conversations and offer manufacturing perspective early in the process
* Strong reporting and documentation discipline
* Willingness and ability to travel extensively to China, including extended stays as needed

* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or related field
* Mandarin fluency strongly preferred
* Experience with connected/IoT consumer products is a strong plus

**About Komline**

As a pioneering leader in advanced separation technologies, Komline has established a global reputation for engineering excellence. Through our combination of innovative design, cutting-edge manufacturing capabilities, and decades of industry experience, we consistently deliver the highest quality equipment from our integrated manufacturing facilities. Serving our core markets of Water & Process, Agricultural & Renewables, and Industrials, we pride ourselves on providing comprehensive separation solutions precisely tailored to our clients' requirements. With a strong track record of strategic growth and acquisitions, Komline continues to expand its solution portfolio and technical capabilities while maintaining our commitment to innovation and customer satisfaction.

**This Opportunity**

The Director, Operational Excellence is responsible for building, deploying, and sustaining the Komline Business System (KBS), a consistent operating excellence system across all Komline sites. This leader will partner with Business Unit General Managers, Plant Managers, and functional leaders to improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, working capital, productivity, and overall operating discipline while respecting the P&L accountability of each business. The role will lead Komline’s enterprise continuous improvement (CI) capability, develop CI talent, and ensure proven practices are shared and scaled across the network.

The successful candidate is a hands-on manufacturing leader who combines strong Lean expertise with business judgment, credibility on the shop floor, and the executive presence to influence decentralized business leaders. This leader will be equally comfortable coaching a plant team, challenging a site improvement plan, and communicating enterprise priorities to senior leadership.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, this enterprise-wide role supports all Komline operating sites.

**Responsibilities:**

* Develop and lead implementation of the KBS Operational Excellence strategy, roadmap, standards, and multi-year improvement agenda across all sites
* Lead, coach, and develop the CI Manager team and other improvement resources; establish clear site coverage, priorities, and deployment expectations
* Partner with GMs and Plant Managers to identify the highest-impact opportunities and build robust, financially validated site-level improvement pipelines that deliver sustained results in safety, productivity, delivery, lead time, quality, inventory, cost, and working capital
* Establish and sustain common Lean / KBS operating practices, including daily management, visual management, standard work, problem solving, RCCM, value-stream improvement, kaizen, and leader standard work
* Create a practical maturity assessment for Operational Excellence and use it to prioritize coaching, capability building, and site support; track improvements in maturity and consistent adoption of core operating practices
* Drive measurable productivity and capacity improvements through flow, labor optimization, constraint removal, setup reduction, layout improvement, and waste elimination
* Partner with Industrial Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, EHS, Finance, Engineering, HR, and other enterprise functions to quantify benefits and ensure improvements are sustained
* Build CI capability within site leadership and frontline teams through training, coaching, kaizen leadership, and development of local change agents
* Establish common operational KPI definitions and review routines that enable benchmarking and the sharing and scaling of best practices across Komline
* Support acquisition integration by assessing operational maturity, identifying improvement opportunities, and integrating acquired sites into Komline’s operating system
* Provide regular enterprise-level reporting to the COO on CI pipeline, benefits realization, site maturity, risks, and resource priorities
* Promote a culture of accountability, structured problem solving, and continuous improvement while maintaining strong partnership with decentralized business leadership

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Business, or a related field
* 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations, continuous improvement, operational excellence, industrial engineering, or related leadership roles
* Demonstrated success leading Lean / continuous improvement across multiple sites or business units
* Strong knowledge of Lean manufacturing, daily management, kaizen, standard work, value-stream mapping, structured problem solving, and performance management
* Proven ability to influence GMs, Plant Managers, and functional leaders without relying on direct authority
* Strong business and financial acumen with the ability to translate operational improvements into measurable financial impact
* Excellent leadership, coaching, facilitation, communication, and executive presentation skills
* Ability to travel approximately 50%+, depending on site and project needs

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Lean leadership certification or equivalent and/or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt
* Experience in multi-site industrial, engineered-product, capital-equipment, or process-equipment manufacturing
* Experience integrating acquired businesses or deploying a common operating system across decentralized businesses
* Experience with plant layout, flow optimization, capacity improvement, and working-capital initiatives
* MBA or advanced technical/operations degree

**Equal Opportunity Statement:**
Komline is an EEO employer – M/F/Vets/Disabled

protected_roles.description:
Global Director, Operational Excellence COE
  
  
At Nouryon, our global team takes positive action every day, to reach higher collectively and individually. We create innovative and sustainable solutions for our customers to answer society’s needs – today and in the future.
  
  
We are looking for team members who bring ideas forward, champion others and work together to do better. Does that sound like you?
  
  
**About the job**
The Global Director, Operational Excellence (OpEx) COE is a senior leadership role responsible for defining the strategic direction, standards, and governance of Nouryon’s global OpEx program. This role owns the organizational design, frameworks, methodologies, and capability pipelines that enable sustainable continuous improvement across 63 manufacturing sites in the Integrated Supply Chain (ISC) organization – spanning the Americas, Europe, and Asia Pacific.
  
  
This role is the architect of OpEx productivity engine. The COE Director owns the design of the systems, standards, and organizational capabilities that enable VMC and FMC delivery – including ownership of the enterprise systems of record for productivity tracking (ANT) and performance reporting (PowerBI). Execution of productivity targets is driven through the regional OpEx Manager network; this role ensures those teams are equipped, aligned, and operating within a governance structure capable of sustaining results.
  
  
This role leads a newly consolidated Center of Excellence that brings together CI methodology and Lean/Six Sigma certification, ISC Learning & Development, End-to-End Process Management, and Manufacturing Excellence under a single governance structure. The COE Director sets priorities, establishes the program architecture, and holds accountability for outcomes – operating through a team of direct reports who own execution across regions. Key relationships span the COO, regional OpEx Managers, Site Directors, and ISC functional leaders across three regions.
  
  
This is a permanent, full-time position reporting to the VP, Global Operational Excellence & Digital Manufacturing, based in a Nouryon regional hub (Amsterdam, Houston, or Shanghai) with global travel of 15–25%.
  
  
**In your future role as the Global Director, Operational Excellence COE, you will**
**CI Methodology, Standards & Governance**

* Own the global Operational Excellence methodology, ensuring a consistent, fit-for-purpose CI framework is deployed across all 63 Nouryon manufacturing sites.

* Define and govern the Lean/Six Sigma certification pathway from Yellow Belt through Master Black Belt, establishing quality standards for program content, assessment, and progression.
* Partner with regional OpEx Managers to translate global standards into site-level execution plans, maintaining strategic alignment while enabling regional adaptation.
* Establish and sustain a durable CI Governance model – defining the review cadence, accountability structure, and performance mechanisms that ensure CI maturity compounds over time across the Nouryon network.
* Own the enterprise systems of record for productivity tracking and performance reporting, including the ANT productivity platform and PowerBI reporting architecture, ensuring data integrity and leadership visibility across all sites.

**ISC Learning & Development**

* Lead the design and continuous improvement of the ISC Learning & Development program, spanning CI capability, technical skills, and leadership development for the ISC organization.
* Direct the L&D team to build and maintain a structured curriculum that supports onboarding, role progression, and organizational capability uplift.
* Connect L&D investment directly to VMC and FMC delivery targets, ensuring program outcomes are measurable and business-relevant.
* Own the design mandate for Digital Literacy and AI capability across the ISC organization – defining the people, process, and metrics framework required to build and sustain enterprise AI competency at scale. This includes establishing program objectives, identifying ownership, and proposing a deployment model aligned to Nouryon’s broader digital strategy.

**End-to-End Process Management**

* Own the ISC End-to-End process architecture, defining process standards, documentation requirements, and governance for core ISC value streams.
* Drive process modeling and SIPOC-level design across ISC, working through the Process Modeler and Global Process Owner to ensure clarity of accountability and performance standards.
* Identify and close process design gaps that create risk, inefficiency, or measurement inconsistency across the ISC organization.

**Manufacturing Excellence**

* Define the Manufacturing Excellence framework for Nouryon, including OEE, TPM, reliability, and asset performance standards applied across the manufacturing network.
* Direct the Manufacturing Excellence Manager to develop and deploy site-level improvement programs, closing the loop between plant performance data and structured intervention.
* Integrate manufacturing excellence priorities into the broader OpEx roadmap, ensuring alignment with Digital Manufacturing, Palantir-enabled analytics, and capital investment decisions.

**People Leadership & COE Development**

* Lead a geographically distributed team of nine direct reports
* Define team structure, role clarity, and succession priorities for the COE
* Build a high-performance COE culture grounded in Nouryon’s Leadership Capability Framework

This role requires approximately 15–25% global travel across the Americas, Europe, and Asia Pacific.
  
  
**Key Performance Indicators**
The Global Director, Operational Excellence COE is measured against the same Breakthrough KPIs as the VP, Global Operational Excellence & Digital Manufacturing. This alignment is intentional – the COE’s organizational design, capability systems, and governance structures exist to enable these outcomes. Execution is driven through the regional OpEx Manager network; this role is accountable for building and sustaining the organization capable of delivering them.
  

* People Safety
* Process Safety
* FMC — Fixed Manufacturing Cost Productivity
* VMC — Variable Manufacturing Cost Productivity
* OEE — Overall Equipment Effectiveness
* OTIF — On-Time In-Full
* Quality Sigma Level
* CI Activation Rate

**We believe you bring**

* A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, or a related discipline; advanced degree preferred.
* A minimum of 15 years of progressive experience in Operational Excellence, Continuous Improvement, or manufacturing leadership roles in a global, multi-site environment.
* Certified Master Black Belt (MBB) or Black Belt in Lean/Six Sigma, with demonstrated capability to design, govern, and quality-assure a full belt certification program.
* Proven track record of leading change management initiatives in large, matrixed, multi-regional organizations – with the ability to align diverse stakeholders and shift organizational culture.
* Deep knowledge of Manufacturing Excellence frameworks including OEE, TPM, and reliability methodologies, with experience deploying these at scale across a manufacturing network.
* Demonstrated people leadership across multiple geographies and organizational grades, including experience developing high-performing teams in a distributed structure.

**Great if you have**

* Experience in specialty chemicals, process manufacturing, or a similarly regulated, capital-intensive industrial environment.
* Hands-on expertise in End-to-End process design and governance, including SIPOC-level architecture and process ownership models.
* Experience designing and leading corporate Learning & Development programs, including competency frameworks and structured curricula for technical disciplines.
* Prior experience building or structuring a Center of Excellence from the ground up, including team design, governance models, and stakeholder alignment.
* Working proficiency with PowerBI or equivalent reporting platforms for program performance tracking and executive communication.

**We believe you are**
...
  
  
A systems thinker who sees the whole before diving into the parts. You lead through frameworks, not firefighting – you understand that durable operational excellence is built on governance, capability, and culture, not individual heroics. You bring intellectual rigor to every conversation and are comfortable challenging assumptions at any level of the organization, including in rooms where the answer is already assumed.
  
  
You are energized by building – building teams, building programs, building the conditions for others to succeed. You know how to hold standards without being rigid, and how to drive urgency without creating chaos. The right candidate is someone who finds genuine satisfaction in watching a global organization improve because of the systems they put in place – and who brings the patience, persistence, and precision that transformation at scale demands.
  
  
**We offer you**
This is a rare opportunity to architect and lead a newly consolidated global COE with a clear mandate from senior leadership, a defined team, and direct line of sight to enterprise value delivery. You will operate with significant autonomy, build the structure you believe is right, and leave a measurable legacy across a global manufacturing organization at an inflection point in its CI and digital transformation journey.
  
  
At Nouryon, we provide a great job and friendly coworkers, plus benefits in addition to salary.
  
  
**Have we got your interest?**
This is a permanent position on a full-time basis, reporting to VP, Global Operational Excellence & Digital Manufacturing, based in a Nouryon regional hub Amsterdam, Netherlands | Houston, TX, USA
  
  
Please apply via our online recruitment system. We will not accept applications via e-mail. Once it's with us we will review to see if we have a match between your skills and the role! For more information about our hiring process, visit: nouryon.com/careers/how-we-hire/
  
  
We look forward to receiving your application!
  
  
We kindly ask our internal candidates to apply with your Nouryon email via Success Factors.
  
  
**About Nouryon**
Explore careers and life at Nouryon
  
  
If you’re looking for your next career move, apply today and join Nouryon’s worldwide team in providing essential solutions that our customers use to manufacture everyday products such as personal care, cleaning, paints and coatings, agriculture and food, pharmaceuticals, and building products. Our employees are driven by the wish to make an impact and actively drive positive change. If that describes you, we will gladly make way for your ambitions. From day one we support you with your personal growth, through challenging positions and comprehensive learning and development opportunities, in a dynamic, international, diverse, and proactive working environment.
  
  
Visit our website and follow us on LinkedIn .
  
  
**#WeAreNouryon #GrowWithUs**

At CAMP Systems, we are the trusted leader in aircraft compliance and health management, proudly serving the global business aviation industry. With over 20,000 aircraft and 33,000 engines supported on our cutting-edge platforms, and partnerships with more than 1,300 maintenance facilities and parts suppliers worldwide, we're shaping the future of aviation technology. Since our founding in 1968, we've grown to a dynamic team of 1,600+ employees across 14 locations globally-all united by a passion for innovation and excellence.
  
  
**Our Mission & Vision:**  
We connect the aviation industry through smart technology to make flight safer and more efficient, driving the future of aviation with intelligence and exceptional customer experiences.
  
  
**Our Values & Excellence Mindset:**  
We are customer obsessed, trust-driven, owners of our work, stronger together, constantly curious, and boldly innovative.
  
  
**What You Will Experience in This Role:**  
  
The Director - Quality Assurance drives quality across CAMP's Aircraft Health Management business and provides quality oversight for data and process quality concerns. The role owns the QMS, the internal audit program, and the full quality escape lifecycle, and serves as CAMP's quality voice with OEMs, regulators, and key customers. The right candidate combines deep aviation maintenance knowledge with a disciplined, data-driven approach to compliance and continuous improvement.
  
  
This is a high-visibility leadership role reporting to the Vice President, Aviation Health Management Operations. The Director partners with senior leaders across a global organization and will build on an established quality program: strengthening the QMS, deepening OEM and customer confidence, and scaling quality practices as AHM grows.
  
  
**Responsibilities:**  
  
**Strategy & Leadership**

* Own and lead quality strategy across the full Aircraft Health Management organization, spanning maintenance tracking and engine health monitoring services, aligned with CAMP's business objectives.
* Serve as the escalation point for quality complaints from customer-facing, maintenance compliance, engine health monitoring, flight scheduling, and inventory functions.
* Partner with senior management and departmental leaders to embed quality methodologies across the organization and lead the associated change management.
* Own the quality budget, resource plan, and tooling (QMS, audit, and corrective action platforms), and build the succession pipeline for the quality team.

**Quality Management System & Certification**

* Own the Quality Management System (QMS) and quality SOPs, driving continuous improvement and ensuring processes meet strict regulatory and OEM requirements.
* Maintain ISO 9001 (or higher) certification for the engine health monitoring business, serving as external certification audit lead and ensuring ongoing audit readiness.
* Lead QMS management review with executive leadership, setting risk-based quality objectives and ensuring consistent QMS implementation (document control, competency records, data integrity) across all AHM locations in North America, Europe, and India.

**Audit & Compliance**

* Own the internal audit program end to end, including audit planning, execution, reporting, and the selection, training, and management of internal auditors.
* Host and manage OEM, customer, and third-party audits, driving findings to timely closure.

**Quality Escapes & Corrective Action**

* Manage all quality escapes from intake through investigation, root cause analysis, corrective and preventive action, and verification of effectiveness, with clear accountability to customers and OEM partners.
* Define and report corrective action performance metrics (e.g., escape rate, time to containment, on-time closure, recurrence) with clear thresholds and escalation paths.

**OEM & Customer Engagement**

* Facilitate and chair weekly, monthly, and quarterly strategic OEM meetings covering quality trends, KPI compliance, and corrective action status.
* Serve as primary quality liaison to OEM partners, regulatory bodies, and high-profile customers and large fleet operators under significant OEM contracts.
* Facilitate weekly, monthly, and quarterly quality reviews with senior management and functional leaders, translating escape, audit, and customer feedback data into trends and strategic quality initiatives.

**Continuous Improvement & Team Leadership**

* Lead process improvement using Lean Six Sigma methods, mentoring teams and driving measurable reductions in escapes, rework, and risk.
* Maintain an executive quality scorecard (customer feedback, escapes, audit results, corrective action performance) to drive data-based decisions.
* Lead, mentor, and develop a team of four, setting priorities and fostering a culture of excellence, accountability, and collaboration.
* Partner with AHM operations, training, and product leaders to ensure analyst competency, training effectiveness, and quality readiness for new products, processes, and teams.

**You have:**

* Bachelor's degree in Aerospace, Engineering, Quality Management, or a related field; advanced degree a plus.
* Minimum of 10 years of proven leadership experience in the aviation or aerospace sector, with senior quality assurance experience preferred.
* Strong working knowledge of aviation maintenance and its regulatory requirements (FAA, EASA, and OEM requirements). Hands-on aviation maintenance experience may offset formal credentials.
* Experience managing quality escapes, investigations, root cause analysis, and corrective action programs.
* Experience owning or managing a QMS in a regulated environment, with working knowledge of ISO 9001 (AS9100 familiarity a plus).
* Strong analytical skills, with the ability to turn quality data into executive-level metrics, insights, and recommendations.
* Excellent communication, negotiation, and presentation skills, with the ability to build relationships with OEMs, customers, and leaders at all levels of the organization.
* Strategic thinking with a strong focus on results and the ability to manage complex projects and initiatives.
* Ability to lead across a multi-site, multi-region team; willingness to travel to CAMP offices, OEM, and customer sites as needed.

**Nice to have:**

* Certified ISO 9001 Internal/External Auditor (or equivalent lead auditor certification) with hands-on audit experience.
* Six Sigma Black Belt, with demonstrated process improvement results.
* Quality manager certification (e.g., ASQ CQM) or Certified Quality Auditor (CQA) is a bonus.
* Experience working with large OEM contracts and high-profile customers or large fleet operators.
* Experience in aircraft maintenance tracking, engine trend monitoring, or other SaaS/data-driven service environments.

**Why Work at CAMP?**  
  
Join a culture where your ideas matter, your impact is real, and your growth is supported. Be part of a team reimagining the future of aviation.

**At Carbon, our mission goes beyond 3D printing. We are enabling creators everywhere to make what the world needs, right now. Our company is built on the idea that diverse fields of study must come together to solve intractable problems. We have grand ambitions to create technology that will influence industry around the world. You will be joining a diverse team with a vibrant culture, where team success is as important as celebrating individual contributions.**

  

**Help us change the world and we will help you change yours.**

  

**Job Description:**

  

We are seeking a Head of Production & Supply Chain Operations to lead our Hardware Production Team and the end-to-end logistics and inventory function that keeps Carbon’s global supply chain running. This role is critical to scaling our production operations while maintaining our commitment to safety, quality, and cost efficiency, while ensuring the accuracy, compliance, and reliable flow of Carbon’s inventory and freight worldwide. The ideal candidate is a disciplined, detail-oriented leader who thrives in a hands-on manufacturing environment, knows how to build, inspire, and motivate high-performing teams, and can operate effectively across both production and supply chain disciplines. Reporting to the Director of Supply Chain, this individual will own the end-to-end production process and the logistics and inventory organization, driving continuous improvement and ensuring our products and materials meet the highest standards from supplier to customer.

  

***This role will be spending time at both our Thomas Rd, Santa Clara and Borregas Ave, Sunnyvale locations and you will be expected to be in-office 5 days per week.***

  

**What You Will Do**

  

**Team Leadership & Development**

* Recruit, hire, onboard, and develop a team of manufacturing technicians and logistics and inventory staff, building a culture rooted in accountability, pride in craftsmanship, and continuous learning.
* Set clear performance expectations and conduct regular coaching sessions, performance reviews, and skills assessments to elevate individual and team capabilities across production and logistics/inventory functions.
* Foster a positive, motivated work environment where team members feel valued and engaged, resulting in strong retention and morale.
Create training programs and cross-training plans to ensure workforce flexibility and depth across all production stations and logistics/inventory operations.  

  

**Safety**

* Champion a safety-first culture across the production floor and logistics and warehouse operations, ensuring compliance with all OSHA regulations and company safety policies.
* Conduct regular safety audits, risk assessments, and incident investigations; implement corrective and preventive actions promptly.
* Develop, maintain, and enforce standard operating procedures (SOPs) that prioritize operator and warehouse safety in every task.
Track and report safety metrics, driving toward zero-incident goals through proactive hazard identification and mitigation.  

  

**Quality**

* Own product quality throughout the manufacturing and assembly process, ensuring every product meets rigorous quality standards before shipment.
* Implement and manage quality control checkpoints, inspection protocols, and testing procedures at critical stages of production.
* Collaborate with Ops Engineering and Quality teams to resolve defects, perform root cause analysis, and drive corrective actions.
Monitor yield rates and first-pass quality metrics, using data to drive continuous improvement initiatives.  

  

**Cost & Operational Efficiency**

* Manage production budgets, labor costs, and material utilization to meet or exceed cost targets without compromising safety or quality.
* Own budget and cost outcomes for Carbon’s freight, logistics, and inventory programs.
* Identify and implement process improvements using Lean manufacturing principles to reduce waste, improve throughput, and increase efficiency.
* Plan and manage production schedules, capacity, and resource allocation to meet delivery commitments and customer demand.
Partner with Strategic Sourcing and Planning to optimize inventory levels and ensure timely availability of components and materials.  

  

**Logistics & Inventory Leadership**

* Own management accountability for the cost, service levels, and integrity of Carbon’s global goods flow, including all inbound and outbound freight and global inventory accuracy and compliance.
* Lead, mentor, and directly manage the team of inventory and logistics staff, setting priorities and building scalable processes as Carbon grows.
* Ensure full compliance with international trade regulations and dangerous goods/hazardous materials requirements.
Establish and track logistics and inventory KPIs (cost per shipment, on-time delivery, inventory accuracy, freight as a percentage of revenue) and drive continuous improvement against them.  

  

**Cross-Functional Collaboration & Reporting**

* Serve as the primary liaison between the production floor and the Engineering, Supply Chain, and Quality teams to ensure seamless product launches and design-for-manufacturability feedback.
* Serve as the primary management point of contact for Finance, Legal, EH&S, Sales, contract manufacturing partners, and 3PLs on logistics, inventory, and trade compliance matters.
* Participate in new product introduction processes, contributing manufacturing insights during design reviews and pilot builds.
Provide regular production, logistics, and inventory status reports, KPIs, and escalation updates to senior leadership.  

  

**Qualifications**

  

**Required:**

* 8+ years of experience in a manufacturing or production management role, with demonstrated success leading teams of technicians or production operators.
* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related field.
* Experience managing, overseeing, or working closely with logistics, freight, and inventory functions, including leading teams responsible for freight and inventory control.
* Proven ability to build, develop, and motivate high-performing teams in a hands-on manufacturing environment, with a track record of maintaining safe production environments.
* Strong technical aptitude with the ability to understand complex electromechanical assemblies and manufacturing processes.
* Demonstrated discipline and meticulous attention to detail in managing production operations, documentation, and quality systems.
* Experience managing budgets, schedules, and resource planning.
Excellent communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills, including the ability to partner effectively with a senior individual-contributor expert to translate strategy into team execution.  

  

**Nice to Have:**

* Understanding of workplace safety regulations (OSHA).
* Lean manufacturing certification (e.g., Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt).
* Experience with ISO 9001 or similar quality management systems.
* Background in 3D printing, additive manufacturing, or precision hardware production.
* Experience with ERP/MRP systems and production tracking tools.
* Familiarity with Design for Manufacturing (DFM) and Design for Assembly (DFA) principles.
Familiarity with international trade compliance and dangerous goods/hazardous materials regulations.
